task_1.title: Support Meson-style static archives in MSBuildDeps
task_1.description: Conan 2.18.0 updates MSBuildDeps so consumers can resolve package libraries produced by Meson when the packaged archive uses the Unix-style lib<name>.a naming convention instead of the default <name>.lib expectation. The generator keeps existing behavior for explicit library filenames and standard .lib-based packages while selecting the Meson archive when that is the actual packaged artifact.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that MSBuildDeps can consume package libraries built with Meson when a dependency declares a bare library name but the packaged archive is exposed as a lib<name>.a file, without breaking existing handling of explicit library filenames or standard .lib libraries.

expectation.grounded: When MSBuildDeps generates dependency properties from cpp_info.libs entries that are provided as bare names, it should continue resolving them to <name>.lib by default, but if the dependency's cpp_info.libdirs contain a Meson-style lib<name>.a archive and do not contain <name>.lib, the generated MSBuildDeps library list should reference lib<name>.a instead. Entries in cpp_info.libs that already include a valid library extension should be preserved as declared. Existing system library handling through cpp_info.system_libs should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: MSBuildDeps should understand both conventional MSBuild library naming and Meson-produced static archive naming for package libraries. Consumers should be able to install dependencies generated by Meson without manually renaming library files, while existing dependency declarations that already work should keep the same observable output.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter the generated name for libraries that already include a supported extension. Do not prefer a Meson archive when a matching <name>.lib file is present in the package library directories. Do not expand this fallback beyond package libraries resolved from cpp_info.libs; behavior for cpp_info.system_libs should stay as before.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be additive and narrowly scoped. It must preserve current behavior for explicit filenames and normal Windows library layouts, and it should only switch to Meson naming when that is the actual packaged artifact being consumed.

behavior: MSBuildDeps now inspects package library directories when converting bare cpp_info.libs entries into generated library filenames.
For a bare library name, the generator still emits <name>.lib unless the package exposes only a Meson-style lib<name>.a archive.
If lib<name>.a exists in the declared package library directories and <name>.lib does not, the generated MSBuildDeps library list uses lib<name>.a.
Library entries that already specify a valid extension remain unchanged in generated MSBuildDeps output.
System library name handling is not changed by this update.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency declares a package library as a bare name and its package library directories contain lib<name>.a but not <name>.lib, generating MSBuildDeps should reference lib<name>.a for that dependency.
When a dependency declares a package library as a bare name and a matching <name>.lib is available, generating MSBuildDeps should continue referencing <name>.lib.
When a dependency declares a package library with an explicit supported extension, generating MSBuildDeps should preserve that declared filename.
When MSBuildDeps processes system libraries, their naming behavior should remain unchanged from previous releases.

task_2.title: Support Meson/MSVC static library names in CMakeDeps
task_2.description: Conan 2.18.0 removes the need to rename Windows static libraries produced by Meson with MSVC when they are consumed through CMakeDeps. It backports older CMake library lookup behavior so archives such as lib-prefixed .a files can satisfy the declared logical library name on CMake versions earlier than 3.29, while preserving normal behavior for unaffected environments.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Windows static libraries produced by Meson with MSVC can be consumed from Conan without renaming the packaged library files, especially when CMakeDeps is used with older CMake releases.

expectation.grounded: When a package declares its library through self.cpp_info.libs using the logical name, CMakeDeps must allow CMake consumers on Windows with non-MinGW toolchains and CMake versions earlier than 3.29 to resolve the packaged library even if the actual artifact uses a lib prefix and a .a static-library suffix. This compatibility should make older CMake-based consumers behave consistently with newer CMake releases, without requiring the package author to rename library files.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to publish and consume Meson/MSVC static libraries on Windows through Conan using their natural artifact names. CMakeDeps should transparently recognize the packaged library for older supported CMake versions so consumers can link dependencies without recipe-side or artifact renaming workarounds.

constraints.grounded: The expanded lookup behavior should apply only to Windows, only when MinGW is not in use, and only for CMake versions below 3.29. Any temporary library prefix or suffix adjustments used to find the package library must be restored immediately after the lookup so unrelated dependency discovery keeps the original CMake search behavior. Existing behavior for newer CMake versions and unaffected platforms must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: This compatibility handling should be narrowly scoped to the environments that need it and must not alter library resolution rules globally. Platforms and toolchains that already work should continue to behave as before.

behavior: CMakeDeps broadens library discovery for Windows non-MinGW consumers running CMake earlier than 3.29 so a requested library name can match Windows import libraries and static archives that use either no prefix or a lib prefix.
A package that advertises a logical library name through Conan metadata can now resolve a packaged static artifact named with a lib prefix and .a suffix without renaming the file.
The compatibility lookup is temporary for each package-library resolution and does not leave modified CMake library prefix or suffix settings in effect afterward.
Consumers using CMake 3.29 or newer, or environments outside the affected Windows non-MinGW case, keep the existing lookup behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan package built on Windows with MSVC exposes a logical library name and ships the corresponding static archive with a lib prefix and .a suffix, a consumer using CMakeDeps with CMake earlier than 3.29 should be able to configure and link against that dependency without renaming the library file.
When the same dependency is consumed in an environment that already supports this naming pattern, the upgrade should not introduce a regression in library resolution.

When CMakeDeps performs the compatibility lookup for one library, later library lookups should continue using the normal CMake search configuration rather than inheriting broadened prefix or suffix rules.
When the consumer is not in the affected Windows non-MinGW and pre-3.29 CMake scenario, dependency discovery should remain behaviorally unchanged.

task_3.title: Model Emscripten thread modes in Conan settings and toolchains
task_3.description: Conan 2.18.0 adds first-class emcc compiler modeling with a threads subset so Emscripten builds can distinguish non-threaded, POSIX-threaded, and Wasm Workers configurations. The upgrade also propagates the corresponding emcc thread flags through generated CMake, Meson, GNU, and Autotools toolchains so compile and link settings stay consistent with the selected threading model.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan models Emscripten threading as part of the `emcc` compiler configuration so binaries built without threads, with POSIX threads, and with Wasm Workers are treated as distinct configurations, and ensure generated toolchains automatically emit the matching compile and link flags for the selected thread mode.

expectation.grounded: Conan should recognize `compiler=emcc` in its default settings model, including a `compiler.threads` subset with `null`, `posix`, and `wasm_workers` values, together with the supported `version`, `libcxx`, `cppstd`, and `cstd` settings for that compiler. For `conan.tools.build.flags.threads_flags()`, `compiler=emcc` with `compiler.threads=posix` should yield `-pthread`, `compiler.threads=wasm_workers` should yield `-sWASM_WORKERS=1`, and any other compiler or unset thread mode should yield no thread-specific flags. `CMakeToolchain`, `MesonToolchain`, `GnuToolchain`, and `AutotoolsToolchain` should propagate these thread flags to both compile and link arguments, while preserving the existing architecture-related flags, including linker-only architecture flags where applicable.
expectation.conceptual: Users configuring Conan for Emscripten should be able to declare the threading model as part of the compiler settings, and Conan should treat that choice as part of the binary identity while automatically generating consistent compiler and linker flags for supported toolchains.

constraints.grounded: No thread-specific flags should be added for non-`emcc` compilers. When `compiler.threads` is unset or `null`, Conan should not emit Emscripten thread flags. Existing architecture, standard library, and other toolchain flags must continue to be emitted alongside any `compiler.threads`-derived flags rather than being replaced or dropped.
constraints.conceptual: This change should only affect Emscripten builds that opt into the new thread-mode setting. Other compilers and non-threaded Emscripten builds should continue to behave as before, and enabling a thread mode should augment normal toolchain generation instead of disrupting it.

behavior: `emcc` is supported as a default Conan compiler setting with explicit `threads` subsettings for unset, POSIX threads, and Wasm Workers modes.
The selected `compiler.threads` value becomes part of how Emscripten binary configurations are distinguished, so incompatible threaded and non-threaded outputs are not treated as interchangeable.
`conan.tools.build.flags.threads_flags()` returns `-pthread` for `compiler.threads=posix`, returns `-sWASM_WORKERS=1` for `compiler.threads=wasm_workers`, and returns no additional flags otherwise.
`CMakeToolchain` appends the `compiler.threads`-derived flag to generated C, C++, shared-linker, and executable-linker flags.

`MesonToolchain`, `GnuToolchain`, and `AutotoolsToolchain` append the `compiler.threads`-derived flag to generated compile and link arguments while retaining existing architecture-related flag handling.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan profile declares `compiler=emcc`, Conan should accept the compiler configuration using the built-in settings model, including `compiler.threads`.
When `compiler=emcc` and `compiler.threads=posix`, supported generated toolchains should include the POSIX threading flag in both compile and link settings.
When `compiler=emcc` and `compiler.threads=wasm_workers`, supported generated toolchains should include the Wasm Workers flag in both compile and link settings.
When `compiler=emcc` is used with different `compiler.threads` values, Conan should treat those builds as different binary configurations rather than as compatible substitutes.
When the compiler is not `emcc`, or when `compiler.threads` is not set, Conan should not introduce Emscripten-specific thread flags into generated toolchains.

task_4.title: Reverse lookup Conan cache references by path
task_4.description: Conan 2.18.0 adds a debugging-oriented reverse lookup that maps a local cache folder path back to the stored recipe or package reference. This lets users and tooling identify which cached artifact owns a given path, including a direct child folder inside that artifact, while failing clearly for unmatched or invalid paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan provides a debugging-friendly way to reverse look up a local cache path with `conan cache ref <path>` and report the cached artifact reference that owns that folder.

expectation.grounded: Expose `conan cache ref <path>` as a read-only cache command, with matching `ConanAPI.cache.path_to_ref(path)` lookup behavior, that resolves a normalized cache-relative path to either a `RecipeReference` or a `PkgReference`. The command should return the matched reference in its no-timestamp string form, search both recipe and package cache records, and retry the immediate parent directory when the supplied path points to a direct subfolder under the stored artifact folder. If the path cannot be resolved relative to the Conan cache root or no cache record matches, it should raise `ConanException` instead of returning a fabricated reference.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to point Conan at a folder from the local cache and see which cached recipe or package it belongs to. The lookup should work for both artifact roots and direct child folders within them, stay read-only, and fail clearly when the path is invalid or does not correspond to any cached artifact.

constraints.grounded: Keep the feature limited to reverse lookup for debugging: it should only inspect existing cache entries, preserve existing cache state, omit timestamp metadata from the displayed reference, and use exact artifact-folder matching with at most one retry on the immediate parent directory.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this as a non-destructive debugging aid. It should identify only real cached artifacts, keep the reported reference format stable and concise, and avoid broad or ambiguous path guessing.

behavior: A new `conan cache ref <path>` cache subcommand accepts a single path argument and returns the reference associated with that cache folder.
Programmatic cache lookups gain `ConanAPI.cache.path_to_ref(path)` with the same path-resolution rules as the CLI command.
Lookup first resolves the supplied path relative to the Conan cache root and normalizes separators before checking stored cache records.
Recipe cache paths resolve to a `RecipeReference`, while package cache paths resolve to a `PkgReference`, and the printed result excludes timestamp data.
If no exact match is found for the supplied path, the lookup retries once using the immediate parent directory so a direct child folder under a cached artifact can still resolve to that artifact.

If path normalization fails, the operation raises `ConanException` for an invalid path; if normalization succeeds but no recipe or package record matches, it raises `ConanException` for a missing cache reference.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan cache ref <path>` with a path to a cached recipe folder, it should print the corresponding recipe reference including its recipe revision and without timestamp data.

When a user runs `conan cache ref <path>` with a path to a cached package folder, it should print the corresponding package reference, preserving package identity and package revision when present, and without timestamp data.

When the supplied path is a direct child folder inside a cached recipe or package directory rather than the stored artifact folder itself, the command should still resolve to the enclosing cached artifact reference.
When the supplied path cannot be normalized relative to the Conan cache root, the command should fail with `ConanException` for an invalid path.
When the supplied path can be normalized but does not match any stored recipe or package entry, the command should fail with `ConanException` instead of returning a reference.

task_5.title: Separate Emscripten linker-only architecture flags in generated toolchains
task_5.description: Conan 2.18.0 now autodetects architecture-specific linker flags from the active profile and routes them only to linker settings in generated toolchains. This prevents Emscripten asm.js builds from receiving a linker-only architecture flag during compilation, while preserving compile-safe architecture flags and thread-related flags where they are required.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan-generated toolchains distinguish architecture flags that are safe for compilation from architecture flags that are linker-only, so Emscripten asm.js profiles link correctly without polluting compile commands, while other architecture- and thread-derived flags continue to be applied in the appropriate stages.

expectation.grounded: For Conan profiles using `compiler=emcc`, architecture-specific flags must be split between `architecture_flag()` and the new `architecture_link_flag()` behavior consumed by generated toolchains. The asm.js Emscripten architecture flag must be emitted only in linker-facing outputs such as CMake shared and executable linker flags, Meson link arguments, and GNU/Autotools `LDFLAGS`, and must not appear in compiler flags. Compile-safe architecture handling must continue to cover cases such as `settings.arch=wasm64`, and thread flags derived from `compiler.threads` must remain propagated to the affected compile and link arguments.
expectation.conceptual: Architecture options inferred from the active profile should be sent to the build stage that actually understands them. Linker-only Emscripten settings should affect only the final link step, while normal architecture and thread settings should keep working across generated toolchains.

constraints.grounded: Do not add linker-only architecture flags to C or C++ compile arguments. Do not regress non-Emscripten architectures or Emscripten targets that do not require a linker-only override. Preserve existing architecture flag emission for compile-safe cases and keep thread-derived flags present in the generated compiler and linker settings for the touched toolchains.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only change where stage-specific flags are applied, not broadly alter unrelated toolchain behavior. Existing builds should continue to receive the same effective architecture and thread configuration unless a linker-only flag needed to be separated from compilation.

behavior: When Conan resolves an Emscripten profile with `settings.arch=asm.js`, it now derives a linker-only architecture flag and applies it only to linker arguments.

Compiler command lines generated for `compiler=emcc` no longer receive the asm.js linker-only flag, avoiding compile-time warnings and warning-as-error build failures caused by passing a linker setting to compilation.
When Conan resolves `compiler=emcc` with `settings.arch=wasm64`, it derives the architecture flag required for 64-bit WebAssembly generation as a regular architecture flag.

CMake, Meson, GNU, and Autotools toolchain outputs now separate compile architecture flags from link-only architecture flags instead of treating all architecture-derived flags as both compile and link flags.
Thread flags derived from `compiler.threads` are included in the generated compile and link settings for the affected toolchains.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan profile uses `compiler=emcc` and `settings.arch=asm.js`, generated toolchains should pass the asm.js architecture override only to linker settings and not to C or C++ compile flags.
When an asm.js build is performed with warnings treated as errors, Conan-generated compiler invocations should not fail because a linker-only architecture flag was injected into compilation.
When a Conan profile uses `compiler=emcc` and `settings.arch=wasm64`, generated toolchains should include the required wasm64 architecture flag wherever regular architecture flags are expected.

When generating CMake, Meson, GNU, or Autotools toolchains from the same profile, each toolchain should preserve the same separation between compile-safe architecture flags, linker-only architecture flags, and thread-related flags.
When the selected compiler and architecture do not require a link-only architecture override, Conan should not add an extra architecture linker flag to the generated toolchain outputs.

task_6.title: Migrate Conan workspaces to list-based package entries
task_6.description: Conan 2.18.0 changes workspace definitions so `conanws.yml` stores editable packages as a list of package objects instead of a reference-keyed map. Workspace resolution now validates or infers each package reference from the package recipe, removes the separate `products` list from the workspace model, and exposes workspace package information in the new list-oriented shape.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan workspaces remain usable after upgrading to 2.18.0 by declaring workspace packages as list entries with a package path and optional reference, without relying on the previous reference-keyed `packages` map or a separate `products` section.

expectation.grounded: `conanws.yml` `packages` and custom `Workspace.packages()` results must follow a list-of-dict contract where each package entry provides `path` and may provide `ref` and `output_folder`. `WorkspaceAPI.packages()` must resolve every entry to a unique `RecipeReference`; if `ref` is omitted it is inferred from the package `conanfile.py`, and `workspace info` must present packages using the new list-style structure with `path` plus optional `ref`.
expectation.conceptual: A Conan workspace should describe editable packages as package entries rather than as a map keyed by reference. Each entry identifies where the editable package lives, may explicitly name its reference, and should still work when the reference can be read from the recipe. Workspace inspection should show the same list-based view that Conan actually uses.

constraints.grounded: Do not accept workspace packages that resolve ambiguously or invalidly: a package entry must point to a location containing `conanfile.py`, any explicit or inferred `RecipeReference` must be valid, and two entries must not resolve to the same reference. Adding the same package path twice must not create duplicate workspace entries. `output_folder` handling must continue to work per package entry, and workspace state must not depend on a separate `products` collection.
constraints.conceptual: The upgraded workspace format must stay unambiguous and safe: every declared package path should correspond to a real editable recipe, package identities must be valid and unique, repeated additions should not duplicate entries, and cleanup or removal should work from the package declarations alone.

behavior: `conanws.yml` now represents `packages` as a list of package objects instead of a mapping from reference string to package metadata.
Each workspace package object can include `path`, optional `ref`, and optional `output_folder`.
When `ref` is missing, Conan resolves the editable package reference by loading the package `conanfile.py` from the declared `path`.
If a package entry points to a path without `conanfile.py`, or its explicit or inferred reference is invalid, workspace package resolution raises `ConanException`.
If multiple package entries resolve to the same `RecipeReference`, Conan raises `ConanException` instead of accepting duplicate editable identities.
`workspace info` presents workspace packages in list form, showing each package path and its reference when one is available, and reports an empty package list as empty rather than as a mapping.

Adding a package stores it as a path-based list entry with its reference, skips duplicate paths instead of creating another entry, and removal or cleanup operates on the package list without a separate `products` section.
acceptance_criteria: When a workspace definition is loaded in Conan 2.18.0, it should treat `packages` as a list of package entries rather than as a reference-keyed mapping.
When a package entry includes both `path` and `ref`, Conan should resolve it as an editable package and expose that package information in workspace inspection output.
When a package entry includes `path` but omits `ref`, Conan should infer the package reference from that package's recipe and resolve it as an editable package.
When a package entry does not contain a valid recipe at its declared path, or its explicit or inferred reference is invalid, Conan should fail with a workspace configuration error.
When two workspace entries resolve to the same package reference, Conan should reject the workspace instead of accepting ambiguous editable packages.
When the same package path is added more than once, the workspace should retain only one package entry for that path.
When a package is removed or workspace cleanup runs, Conan should act on the package entries declared in `packages` without requiring a separate products list.

task_7.title: Support editable executable targets in CMakeConfigDeps
task_7.description: Conan 2.18.0 extends CMakeConfigDeps so editable packages can expose executable artifacts correctly, including Windows executables with a .exe suffix. The update preserves editable artifact metadata such as executable name and resolved location when Conan merges editable package information with package metadata, allowing generated CMake config files to point consumers at the editable binary output instead of losing that executable information.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps supports executable artifacts from editable packages, including Windows .exe outputs, so consumers can discover and use those executables through generated CMake package configuration the same way they can for non-editable packages.

expectation.grounded: When editable package metadata is merged into the dependency model used by CMakeConfigDeps, scalar artifact fields exposed through cpp_info must be preserved for editable consumption. In particular, cpp_info.exe, cpp_info.location, cpp_info.link_location, cpp_info.type, and cpp_info.languages defined through editable package metadata must override prior merged values when present, so generated CMake config files can emit imported executable targets that use the editable artifact path, including executable filenames ending in .exe.
expectation.conceptual: Editable Conan dependencies that provide executables should behave like packaged dependencies when consumed from CMakeConfigDeps. If a package declares an executable and its location for editable development, downstream CMake consumers should receive a usable imported executable target that resolves to the actual built executable, including platform-specific .exe filenames on Windows.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing merge behavior for multi-value cpp_info metadata and dependency requirements unchanged. Treat the executable-related artifact fields as single-value metadata: overwrite only when the editable definition provides a non-null value, do not concatenate them, and do not erase previously available package metadata when the editable definition omits a field.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only improve editable artifact resolution. It must not break existing dependency metadata merging, and missing editable-specific executable details should fall back to the normal package information instead of causing loss of previously available artifact data.

behavior: Editable metadata now carries scalar artifact information for executable consumption through the merge path used before CMakeConfigDeps generation.
If editable metadata defines an executable name or artifact location, those editable values take precedence over previously merged package values.
Executable-related scalar metadata is treated as overwrite-only configuration rather than appendable metadata.
If editable metadata does not define one of the executable-related scalar fields, the existing merged package value remains available.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan dependency is used in editable mode and declares an executable artifact for CMakeConfigDeps, the generated CMake package configuration should expose a usable imported executable target for that dependency.
When the editable executable file includes a .exe suffix, consumer CMake configuration should resolve and use that executable path without requiring the user to strip or rename the extension.
When editable metadata provides an explicit executable location, the generated dependency configuration should use that editable location rather than losing it during metadata merge.
When editable metadata omits executable-specific fields, consumers should still retain the previously available package metadata instead of ending up with missing executable artifact information.

task_8.title: Support custom build directories in basic_layout
task_8.description: The upgrade adds an optional way to choose the build output directory used by basic_layout, including out-of-source locations, while keeping the existing default layout behavior for recipes that do not opt in.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `basic_layout` lets recipe authors override the build output directory, including using a path outside the source tree, while preserving the current default layout when no custom build folder is requested.

expectation.grounded: `conan.tools.layout.basic_layout()` should accept an optional `build_folder` argument. When a non-empty `build_folder` is supplied, the resolved `conanfile.folders.build` should use that value instead of the default `build` or `build-<build_type>` naming, and `conanfile.folders.generators` should continue to resolve under the chosen build directory. If `conanfile.folders.subproject` is set, relative custom build folders should resolve within that subproject context. When `build_folder` is not supplied, existing source and build folder behavior should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to choose the name or location of the build directory used by `basic_layout`, including out-of-source builds, without affecting recipes that continue to use the default layout.

constraints.grounded: The change must be additive and backward-compatible for existing calls to `basic_layout(conanfile)` and calls that only override `src_folder`. Supplying `build_folder` should only affect build directory resolution and dependent generator placement; omitting it should preserve the prior automatic build directory naming, including build-type-specific suffixes and subproject-aware defaults.
constraints.conceptual: Existing recipes should behave the same unless they opt into a custom build folder. Choosing a custom build location should not alter unrelated layout behavior beyond where build and generator outputs are placed.

behavior: `basic_layout` exposes a new optional `build_folder` parameter.
When `build_folder` is provided, the build directory resolves to that custom path instead of the default build directory name.
When a custom `build_folder` is used, the automatic `build_type` suffix is not added to the build directory.
When a subproject layout is active, relative custom build folders resolve under the configured subproject path.
Generator files continue to be placed inside a `conan` subdirectory beneath the resolved build directory.
When `build_folder` is omitted, the previous default behavior remains, including the standard build directory naming rules.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe calls `basic_layout(self)` without `build_folder`, it should keep using the default build directory naming convention, including any `build_type` suffix that previously applied.
When a recipe calls `basic_layout(self, build_folder="custom_build_folder")`, it should use `custom_build_folder` as the build directory and place generator output under `custom_build_folder/conan`.
When a recipe defines `folders.subproject` and passes a relative `build_folder`, the resolved build directory should be located inside that subproject.
When a recipe passes an out-of-source path through `build_folder`, the layout should allow build and generator outputs to resolve to that location.
When a recipe customizes `src_folder` but does not set `build_folder`, the source folder behavior should remain unchanged from previous versions.

task_9.title: Allow PkgConfigDeps to skip package-level .pc generation
task_9.description: Conan 2.18.0 adds an opt-out in PkgConfigDeps so packages can set `pkg_config_name` to `"none"` and suppress generation of the package-level pkg-config file. This avoids exposing an extra top-level `.pc` entry when only specific pkg-config files should be public.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `PkgConfigDeps` lets a package opt out of generating its package-level pkg-config file by setting `pkg_config_name` to `"none"`, so consumers only receive the intended public `.pc` files.

expectation.grounded: When `PkgConfigDeps` processes a dependency whose package-level `pkg_config_name` property is `"none"`, it should interpret that value as a skip signal and not create the dependency's main `.pc` file. Existing pkg-config generation behavior should otherwise remain intact, including generation of any remaining `.pc` files and dependency metadata derived from those generated entries.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare that a package has no public top-level pkg-config entry. In that case, `PkgConfigDeps` should omit the package's main `.pc` file while continuing to generate and connect any other valid pkg-config outputs.

constraints.grounded: The `"none"` sentinel applies to the dependency-level `pkg_config_name` property used to decide whether to create the main package `.pc` file. The change must not expose `"none"` as a pkg-config dependency name, must not rename unrelated generated `.pc` files, and must not alter packages that do not request the opt-out except for omission of the skipped main file.
constraints.conceptual: Skipping the top-level pkg-config file should be a narrow opt-out. It must not create fake dependency names, disturb unrelated pkg-config outputs, or change behavior for packages that do not enable this setting.

behavior: If a dependency's package-level `pkg_config_name` is `"none"`, `PkgConfigDeps` does not generate that dependency's main `.pc` file.
Generated pkg-config dependency metadata should be based on the remaining available `.pc` entries and should not reference the skipped top-level package file.
The reserved value `"none"` is treated as a request to skip the package-level pkg-config output rather than as a literal public pkg-config name.
acceptance_criteria: When a package sets its package-level `pkg_config_name` to `"none"` and a consumer runs `PkgConfigDeps`, the package's top-level `.pc` file should not be generated.
When other generated `.pc` files depend on that package, their dependency metadata should not reference the skipped package file or expose `"none"` as a dependency name.
When a package does not set `pkg_config_name` to `"none"`, `PkgConfigDeps` should continue generating the package-level `.pc` file as before.
When a package still exposes valid remaining pkg-config outputs, those `.pc` files should continue to be generated and remain usable even if the package-level file is skipped.

task_10.title: Support SBOM and lockfile inputs in conan audit list
task_10.description: `conan audit list` now supports auditing dependencies from CycloneDX SBOM files and Conan lockfiles in addition to direct references and package lists. This expands vulnerability lookup to dependency metadata artifacts while keeping the command limited to one explicit input source per invocation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan audit list` can list vulnerabilities from a CycloneDX SBOM file or a Conan lockfile, while preserving existing direct reference and package list support and requiring exactly one input source per invocation.

expectation.grounded: `conan audit list` shall accept exactly one of: a `reference` argument, `--list`, `--sbom`, or `--lockfile`. With `--sbom`, it shall load the SBOM, accept only documents whose `bomFormat` is `CycloneDX`, extract Conan package references from component `purl` entries, and audit those references. With `--lockfile`, it shall load the lockfile, collect the entries in `requires`, normalize them as Conan `RecipeReference` values, and audit those references. Existing `reference` and `--list` behavior shall remain available.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run `conan audit list` against a single package reference, a package list, a CycloneDX SBOM, or a lockfile and receive vulnerability information for the dependencies represented by that input. Unsupported SBOM formats should be rejected clearly instead of being interpreted as valid audit input.

constraints.grounded: The input modes for `conan audit list` must remain mutually exclusive and mandatory. The command must continue using the selected audit provider and existing audit flow for direct references and package list files. Non-CycloneDX SBOM input must fail explicitly, and package list input that contains no recipe revisions must continue to warn instead of crashing.
constraints.conceptual: Each invocation should accept one explicit source of dependency data. Existing audit workflows must stay compatible, and invalid or unsupported artifact formats must fail safely rather than producing misleading vulnerability results.

behavior: `conan audit list --sbom <file>` audits the Conan package references declared in the SBOM components.
SBOM input is supported only for CycloneDX documents; other SBOM formats are rejected with an error.
`conan audit list --lockfile <file>` audits every required recipe reference stored in the lockfile.
The command rejects invocations that omit an input source or provide more than one of `reference`, `--list`, `--sbom`, and `--lockfile`.
Direct-reference and package-list auditing remain supported, and package lists without recipe revisions still produce a warning instead of vulnerability results.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan audit list --sbom <cyclonedx-file>`, it should return vulnerability results for the Conan package references represented by the SBOM components.
When a user runs `conan audit list --sbom <file>` with an SBOM whose format is not CycloneDX, the command should fail with an unsupported-format error.
When a user runs `conan audit list --lockfile <file>`, it should return vulnerability results for each required recipe reference contained in the lockfile.
When a user invokes `conan audit list` without any input source, or combines one input source with another, the command should reject the invocation because exactly one input source is allowed.
When a user audits a direct reference or a package list, the existing behavior should continue to work, and a package list with no recipe revisions should emit a warning rather than crash.

task_12.title: Shared install-strip config for CMake and Meson
task_12.description: Version 2.18.0 introduces a shared install-strip configuration for CMake and Meson install helpers, while retaining the older CMake-only setting as a deprecated compatibility path. This gives users one cross-tool way to request stripped install artifacts and warns CMake users who still rely on the legacy key.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that install-time stripping can be configured consistently across both CMake and Meson workflows, and that existing CMake consumers using the legacy install-strip configuration continue to get stripped installs while being notified to migrate.

expectation.grounded: `CMake.install()` and `Meson.install()` must honor `tools.build:install_strip` as the shared boolean configuration for install-time stripping. `CMake.install()` must continue to accept `tools.cmake:install_strip` for backward compatibility, emit a deprecation warning when that legacy key is used, and still perform stripping when either configuration is enabled.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to turn on stripped installs through one shared configuration across supported build helpers. Existing CMake projects that still use the older setting should keep working for now, but they should receive a clear deprecation signal telling them to move to the shared option.

constraints.grounded: Default install behavior must remain unchanged when no install-strip configuration is enabled. CMake stripping support must not regress during the deprecation period, and using only `tools.build:install_strip` must not trigger the legacy deprecation warning. Meson support should be additive through the shared configuration rather than requiring a CMake-specific setting.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change install behavior unless stripping is explicitly requested. Keep current CMake users working during migration, avoid deprecation noise for users already on the new shared setting, and extend the same stripping capability to Meson without introducing tool-specific migration burdens.

behavior: `tools.build:install_strip` is introduced as a built-in configuration for controlling install-time stripping across supported build helpers.
`CMake.install()` adds stripping to the install invocation when `tools.build:install_strip` is enabled.
`Meson.install()` adds stripping to the install invocation when `tools.build:install_strip` is enabled.
`CMake.install()` still honors `tools.cmake:install_strip`; when that deprecated key is enabled, it emits a deprecation warning and still performs install-time stripping.
For CMake, enabling either the new shared configuration or the deprecated CMake-specific configuration results in stripped installation output.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer enables `tools.build:install_strip` and runs a CMake install, the install should execute in stripped mode.
When a consumer enables `tools.build:install_strip` and runs a Meson install, the install should execute in stripped mode.
When a consumer enables `tools.cmake:install_strip` and runs a CMake install, the install should still execute in stripped mode and surface a deprecation warning for that configuration.
When a consumer uses only `tools.build:install_strip`, no deprecation warning about `tools.cmake:install_strip` should be emitted.
When no install-strip configuration is enabled, CMake and Meson installs should preserve their prior non-stripping behavior.

task_11.title: Add first-class Emscripten emcc and wasm64 support
task_11.description: Conan 2.18.0 adds first-class Emscripten support by recognizing the emcc compiler, introducing wasm64 as a supported architecture, and producing consistent standards, standard-library, architecture, linker, and cross-toolchain metadata for Emscripten web targets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan treats Emscripten as a first-class target by accepting emcc-based profiles, supporting wasm, asm.js, and wasm64 architectures, and generating the correct observable compiler, linker, standards, and target-metadata behavior for those web builds.

expectation.grounded: Conan must accept `compiler=emcc` as a valid compiler setting with `version=ANY`, `libcxx`, `threads`, `cppstd`, and `cstd` domains appropriate for Emscripten, and it must accept `arch=wasm64` alongside existing `wasm` and `asm.js` targets. For emcc builds, `conan.tools.build.libcxx_flags()` must honor `compiler.libcxx`, `architecture_flag()` must add the Emscripten-visible 64-bit memory mode signal for `arch=wasm64`, and `architecture_link_flag()` must add the asm.js output-forcing signal for `arch=asm.js`. `conan.tools.build.supported_cppstd()` and `supported_cstd()` must report emcc-supported standards according to emcc version ranges rather than generic clang version parsing. Toolchain metadata helpers that derive architecture names or triplets must recognize `wasm64` as a valid target.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare Emscripten builds with emcc and web-target architectures directly in Conan profiles, and Conan should consistently understand those targets, expose the right language-standard availability for the selected emcc version, and emit the observable build and link settings needed for wasm64 and asm.js outputs.

constraints.grounded: Existing `wasm` and `asm.js` support must remain valid, emcc-specific architecture or linker signals must only appear for matching emcc target combinations, standard availability must remain version-gated for emcc, and the added target recognition must not broaden unrelated compilers or architectures.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should extend web-target support without changing unrelated platform behavior, and it should stay conservative by only enabling target-specific flags and standards when the selected compiler and architecture actually require them.

behavior: `arch=wasm64` becomes a recognized Conan architecture for Emscripten-targeted builds.
`compiler=emcc` becomes a recognized compiler setting with configurable version, standard library, thread model, C++ standard, and C standard values for Emscripten profiles.
When the target is `compiler=emcc` with `arch=wasm64`, Conan emits the architecture-specific signal that enables 64-bit WebAssembly memory mode.
When the target is `compiler=emcc` with `arch=asm.js`, Conan emits the linker-specific signal that disables WASM output and forces asm.js output.
When `compiler=emcc` uses `compiler.libcxx`, Conan generates clang-like standard-library selection flags and the corresponding GNU C++11 ABI define behavior where applicable.
`supported_cppstd()` and `supported_cstd()` return emcc-specific supported standards based on emcc version bands, allowing newer emcc versions to expose newer language standards.
Helpers that translate Conan architectures into Meson CPU families, Qbs architecture values, and GNU triplets recognize `wasm64` instead of treating it as unsupported.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan profile declares `os=Emscripten`, `compiler=emcc`, and `arch=wasm64`, Conan should accept the settings as valid rather than rejecting the compiler or architecture.
When Conan computes build flags for an emcc target with `arch=wasm64`, the resulting architecture-related flags should request 64-bit WebAssembly memory mode.
When Conan computes link flags for an emcc target with `arch=asm.js`, the resulting linker flags should force asm.js output instead of default WASM output.
When an emcc profile selects `compiler.libcxx=libc++` or a libstdc++ variant, Conan should emit observable standard-library selection behavior consistent with that choice.
When consumers query `supported_cppstd()` or `supported_cstd()` for emcc, the returned standards should reflect the selected emcc version range rather than a generic non-emcc compiler rule.
When Conan generates cross-build metadata for a `wasm64` target, the derived architecture names or triplets should identify `wasm64` as a valid web target.

task_13.title: Add local file opening support to TestClient
task_13.description: Version 2.18.0 adds user-facing helper methods on TestClient for opening generated local files with the operating system's default application. The feature supports files in the current test workspace and in the client home/cache area, while explicitly preventing this behavior in CI environments.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that local Conan test workflows can open generated files directly from TestClient, including files created in the current test workspace and files stored in the client home/cache area, while refusing to perform interactive file opening in CI environments.

expectation.grounded: TestClient should expose an open(filename) operation that resolves the target relative to the client's current working folder and launches it with the host platform's default file opener. TestClient should also expose open_home(filename) for targets under the client home/cache folder. In CI environments, attempting to use this feature should fail immediately with an assertion-style error instead of trying to launch a local application.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to ask the test client to open files it created on disk using the normal desktop application for their operating system. The same convenience should work for files in the test workspace and in the client's home/cache location, but the feature must be unavailable in non-interactive CI runs.

constraints.grounded: The feature must remain local-only and side-effect driven: it opens an existing filesystem path through the operating system rather than reading file contents or returning them. Path resolution for open(filename) is based on the current test folder, and path resolution for open_home(filename) is based on the client home/cache folder. The behavior must respect Windows, macOS, and other desktop platforms via their native file-opening mechanisms, and it must not silently run in CI.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability should only trigger the machine's normal file-opening behavior for local files and should preserve clear separation between workspace files and client-home files. It should behave appropriately across supported desktop operating systems and avoid attempting interactive UI actions in automated environments.

behavior: A new TestClient.open(filename) capability opens a file located relative to the client's current working directory.
A new TestClient.open_home(filename) capability opens a file located relative to the client's home/cache directory.
On Windows, the file is opened through the system's standard file-launch behavior.
On macOS, the file is opened through the platform's default open command.
On Linux and other non-Windows, non-macOS environments, the file is opened through the platform's standard desktop opener.
If the CI environment variable is set, invoking the open capability raises an assertion-style failure instead of launching the file.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer calls TestClient.open with a relative path to a file in the current test workspace during a local interactive run, the file should be opened by the operating system's default associated application.

When a consumer calls TestClient.open_home with a relative path to a file stored under the client home/cache area during a local interactive run, the file should be opened by the operating system's default associated application.
When the feature is used on Windows, it should rely on the platform's normal file-launch behavior rather than a Conan-specific viewer.
When the feature is used on macOS or Linux-like desktops, it should invoke the platform's normal file-opening command for the resolved path.
When the CI environment variable is present, calling either opening path should fail immediately with an assertion-style error and should not attempt to open any local application.

task_15.title: Add profile Jinja rendering context
task_15.description: Profile templates can now detect whether they are being rendered for host resolution, build resolution, or without an explicit role. The new context signal is available during Jinja2 rendering, is preserved across included profiles, and is exposed through profile-loading APIs so a single template can adapt its behavior by profile role without changing existing profile precedence.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Jinja2-rendered profiles can detect whether they are being evaluated as a host profile, a build profile, or without an explicit profile role, so users can author profile templates that adapt settings, options, or configuration to the active resolution context.

expectation.grounded: Profile Jinja2 rendering must expose a `context` template variable. When Conan resolves dual profiles, the host profile render pass must receive `context="host"` and the build profile render pass must receive `context="build"`. When profiles are loaded through `ProfilesAPI.get_profile()` without an explicit role, the render value must remain `None`. The same `context` value must be preserved when rendering included profiles loaded through profile inheritance.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to branch inside a profile template based on whether the profile is being used for host resolution, build resolution, or a generic single-profile operation. That role information should stay consistent across the full profile expansion, including any included profiles.

constraints.grounded: Adding `context` to the Jinja render environment must not change profile composition order, CLI override precedence, or the availability of the existing template variables already exposed during profile rendering. Profiles that do not reference `context` should continue to render as before.
constraints.conceptual: This feature should add role-awareness to profile templates without altering existing profile merging behavior or breaking templates that ignore the new variable.

behavior: Jinja2 profile templates receive a new `context` variable during rendering.
Profiles rendered as host profiles expose `context` as `"host"`.
Profiles rendered as build profiles expose `context` as `"build"`.
Profiles loaded without an explicit host/build role expose `context` as `None`.
Included profiles are rendered with the same `context` value as the profile that included them.
Programmatic profile resolution through `ProfilesAPI.get_profile()` accepts an explicit render context.
acceptance_criteria: When a command resolves both host and build profiles, a Jinja condition on `context` should be able to produce different rendered content for the host and build profile passes.
When a profile includes another profile, both the including and included templates should observe the same `context` value during the same resolution flow.
When a profile is rendered outside a host/build split, a Jinja condition should be able to detect the absence of an explicit role via `context` evaluating as `None`.
When a profile template does not use `context`, its rendered result and normal profile override behavior should remain unchanged from prior versions.

task_14.title: Orchestrated workspace package creation
task_14.description: Conan 2.18.0 introduces a workspace-level create flow that exports workspace recipes, computes dependency order across selected packages, and creates results in the Conan cache instead of treating workspace members as local editables. The update also adds a workspace source command, aligns workspace package discovery with the declared workspace packages, and preserves quoted forwarded arguments when nested Conan commands are executed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan workspaces can orchestrate creation of selected workspace packages into the Conan cache in correct dependency order, using the active profile, lockfile, remote, and build context, and provide a workspace-level way to run package source retrieval.

expectation.grounded: `conan workspace create` must export workspace recipes, resolve the selected workspace packages via `WorkspaceAPI.packages()` and `--pkg` reference matching, compute a merged build order from each selected package's dependency graph with the active profiles, remotes, build modes, update flag, and lockfile inputs, temporarily disable workspace editable interception, and then invoke `conan create` for workspace members and `conan install` for external dependencies that need building. `conan workspace source` must execute each selected workspace package's `source()` using its declared reference metadata and available remotes. Forwarded nested commands must preserve shell-style quoted arguments.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to create some or all packages from a workspace as cache packages, not local editables, and have Conan determine the right order automatically from the dependency graph, including required external builds and host/build context differences. Users should also be able to trigger source retrieval for selected workspace packages directly from the workspace CLI, and quoted arguments should continue to work when the workspace command delegates to other Conan commands.

constraints.grounded: `conan workspace create` must only operate on workspace packages selected by the `--pkg` filters, raise an error if the selection is empty, skip nodes whose binary state does not require building, keep workspace-created results in the Conan cache instead of local editable locations, and preserve package reference identity including name, version, user, and channel when delegating `conan create`. Build-require packages must be delegated with build-context create semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The orchestration should not silently do nothing for an invalid package selection, should not rebuild packages that are already resolved, should not confuse cache creation with editable workspace builds, and should respect the distinction between normal requirements and build requirements.

behavior: Adds a `conan workspace create` command that orchestrates workspace package creation in dependency order and stores created packages in the Conan cache.
Before orchestrating creates, workspace recipes are exported so selected workspace references are available to dependency resolution and can be treated as buildable when missing.
Workspace package selection supports repeated `--pkg` filters matched against workspace recipe references, and the command fails when no workspace packages are selected.
Build order is computed by loading and merging dependency graphs for the selected workspace packages with the active host/build profiles, remotes, build mode, update flag, and lockfile inputs.

During orchestration, external dependencies that require building are delegated through nested Conan install/build actions, while workspace members are delegated through nested Conan create actions using their reference metadata.
Only package nodes in build-required states are executed; other binary states are skipped instead of being rebuilt.
Adds a `conan workspace source` command that executes the `source()` method for each selected workspace package.
Nested command dispatch now preserves quoted arguments and paths when workspace commands invoke other Conan commands.
acceptance_criteria: When a workspace contains multiple interdependent packages and the user runs `conan workspace create`, the packages should be created in dependency order and the resulting packages should be produced in the Conan cache rather than as active local editable builds.

When `conan workspace create` is run with profiles, build modes, remotes, update settings, or lockfile inputs, the computed build order and delegated create/install actions should use that same context.
When selected workspace packages depend on external packages that must be built, `conan workspace create` should build those external dependencies before creating dependent workspace packages.
When `--pkg` filters are provided, `conan workspace create` should restrict orchestration to matching workspace references; if nothing matches, it should fail with a selection error.
When a dependency node is already resolved and does not require a build, `conan workspace create` should skip rebuilding it.
When a selected workspace package is used as a build requirement, the orchestration should create it in build context rather than treating it as a normal host requirement.
When the user runs `conan workspace source`, the selected workspace packages should execute their `source()` methods.
When delegated workspace commands include quoted paths or arguments, those arguments should be preserved correctly during nested command execution.

task_17.title: Support cpp_info.sources in CMakeConfigDeps targets
task_17.description: Conan 2.18.0 adds source-target support to CMakeConfigDeps by honoring source files declared through cpp_info.sources. Generated imported CMake targets now propagate those packaged sources as configuration-aware interface sources, so source-based dependencies can be consumed without extra manual target wiring.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps exposes source-based dependency metadata so packages that declare cpp_info.sources are consumed as CMake source targets through the generated dependency targets.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps generates a target from a cpp_info entry that defines sources, it should resolve each declared source against the package folder and append the resulting paths to the generated imported target's INTERFACE_SOURCES property. This source metadata should be emitted through the generator's configuration-aware wrapping and should coexist with the existing include directories, compile definitions, compile options, link flags, and system library metadata.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers using CMakeConfigDeps should automatically receive dependency source files declared by the package as part of the dependency target interface, enabling source-target consumption through normal CMake target usage.

constraints.grounded: The change must be additive to CMakeConfigDeps target generation. It must not alter target type or unrelated metadata emission, and it should only add INTERFACE_SOURCES when cpp_info.sources is present and non-empty. Dependencies without declared sources should continue to generate the same target metadata they produced before.
constraints.conceptual: The new source-target support should not disturb existing dependency target behavior. Packages that do not declare sources should behave exactly as before, and packages that do declare sources should gain source propagation without losing other dependency metadata.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps reads source entries declared in cpp_info.sources and carries them into the generated target description.
Each declared source file is converted into a package-resolved path before it is emitted to CMake.
Generated imported targets append declared source files to INTERFACE_SOURCES instead of treating them as link libraries or other link metadata.
The emitted source list is configuration-aware, matching the generator's existing per-configuration target emission behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency declares one or more cpp_info.sources entries and a consumer generates files with CMakeConfigDeps, the resulting imported CMake target should expose those files through INTERFACE_SOURCES.
When declared source entries refer to packaged files using relative paths, the generated target should reference package-resolved paths rather than unresolved raw relative strings.
When multiple source files are declared for a generated dependency target, all declared files should be propagated to that target's interface sources.
When no cpp_info.sources are declared, the generated CMakeConfigDeps target output should remain unchanged apart from the absence of source-target metadata.

task_16.title: Expose `cpp_info.sources` in CMakeConfigDeps
task_16.description: Conan 2.18.0 adds `cpp_info.sources` so recipes can publish packaged source files as dependency metadata, and CMake consumers using `CMakeConfigDeps` can receive those files on generated package and component targets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recipes can declare packaged source files as dependency metadata and that consumers using `CMakeConfigDeps` receive those files on the generated dependency target, including component targets.

expectation.grounded: Support a list-valued `sources` field on `CppInfo` at both `self.cpp_info.sources` and `self.cpp_info.components[<name>].sources`. Conan should preserve this metadata through normal `CppInfo` serialization and merging, and `CMakeConfigDeps` should expose the declared packaged source paths on the generated target for the corresponding package or component by populating CMake source-target metadata such as `INTERFACE_SOURCES`.
expectation.conceptual: Packages should be able to publish source files as part of their public CMake-facing metadata. When a consumer installs such a dependency with Conan's CMake dependency generator, the imported dependency target should carry those source files so CMake can treat the dependency as a source target. The same capability should work for both the main package target and named components.

constraints.grounded: `sources` must remain optional, defaulting to no source entries when unset. Adding source-target support must not remove or alter existing include directory, library, framework, flag, requirement, or executable metadata, and package or component targets that do not declare `sources` should continue to generate as before.
constraints.conceptual: Existing packages should keep their current behavior unless they opt in to publishing source files. Source metadata should augment generated dependency targets without regressing existing link, include, or component behavior.

behavior: `CppInfo` now exposes a `sources` list at both package scope and component scope.
Declared `sources` entries are retained when `CppInfo` is serialized or merged, so source metadata survives normal Conan package metadata handling.
`CMakeConfigDeps` resolves declared source paths against the packaged dependency content and associates them with the generated imported target for the matching package or component.
Generated CMake targets append declared source files to configuration-aware source-target metadata instead of ignoring them.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe assigns packaged source paths to `self.cpp_info.sources` and the dependency is consumed through `CMakeConfigDeps`, the generated package target should expose those files as CMake source metadata for the active configuration.

When a recipe assigns packaged source paths to `self.cpp_info.components[<name>].sources`, the generated target for that component should expose those files as CMake source metadata for the active configuration.
When `sources` is not declared for a package or component, generated CMake targets should behave the same as before and should not gain source metadata.
When Conan persists or merges package metadata, declared `sources` entries should remain available to downstream generators.

task_20.title: Improve CMakeDeps errors for invalid component requirements
task_20.description: Conan 2.18.0 improves the failure mode in CMakeDeps/CMakeConfigDeps when a recipe declares cpp_info.requires against a dependency component that does not exist. Invalid package::component references now fail with an explicit Conan configuration error that identifies the missing component and package, while valid root-package references continue to resolve normally.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeDeps reports an actionable user-facing error when a recipe declares an incorrect component requirement for another package, instead of failing with a generic internal assertion, while preserving support for valid root-package requirements.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps processes cpp_info.requires entries of the form package::component, it should distinguish between a valid root-package target (package::package) and a missing dependency component. If the referenced component does not exist and the request is not the package root target, generation should raise ConanException describing that the requested component is not present in the referenced package.
expectation.conceptual: If a package recipe points CMakeDeps at a dependency component that does not exist, the generator should fail with a clear configuration error that tells the user which package/component reference is invalid. Valid references to the dependency's top-level target should continue to work as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing handling of package-root requirements where the required package name and component token are the same. Only invalid cross-package component references with no matching component should switch from an assertion-style failure to an explicit Conan configuration error.
constraints.conceptual: Keep successful dependency generation unchanged for valid package-level references, and only improve the error behavior for misdeclared component dependencies.

behavior: When a recipe declares cpp_info.requires for another package using package::component, CMakeConfigDeps now verifies whether the named component exists in that dependency before treating it as a special case.
If the named component is missing and the reference is not the package's own root target, dependency generation fails with ConanException instead of a generic assertion failure.
The reported failure explicitly identifies the recipe making the request, the requested package/component reference, and the dependency package in which the component could not be found.
References to the dependency root target using the package name as both sides of the package::package reference remain accepted and continue through the existing default-target path.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer recipe declares cpp_info.requires with a dependency component name that does not exist, running CMakeDeps/CMakeConfigDeps should stop with a Conan configuration error rather than an internal assertion-style crash.
When that error is raised, it should make clear which package::component reference is invalid and which dependency package is missing that component.
When a consumer recipe declares a valid root-package requirement in the form package::package, CMakeDeps/CMakeConfigDeps should continue generating targets without introducing a new error.

task_18.title: Add Conan recipe diff reporting
task_18.description: Conan 2.18.0 adds a new `conan report diff` command that compares two recipe versions or revisions, including their exported and configured source content, and can render the result as plain text, structured JSON, or a searchable HTML report. The command can compare cached or remote references, or local recipe paths paired with references, and resolves missing revisions automatically when possible.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can inspect the differences between two Conan recipes, including recipe revisions or versions and their associated source content, through a dedicated reporting command that works for both reference-based and local-path comparisons and produces usable human-readable or machine-readable output.

expectation.grounded: Provide a `conan report diff` command backed by `ConanAPI.report.diff` that accepts required `--old-reference` and `--new-reference` inputs plus optional `--old-path`, `--new-path`, and repeated `--remote` arguments. When a side is given only as a reference, resolve it from the local cache and enabled remotes, and if no recipe revision is supplied, select the latest available recipe revision. When a side is given as a local path plus reference, export that recipe under the supplied reference identity and compare it without requiring a pre-existing cached or remote revision for that side. The command must generate a diff covering the recipe export area together with configured exported/source content, and support `text`, `json`, and `html` formatters. The `text` formatter should emit the raw diff, the `json` formatter should emit a file-grouped structured diff payload, and the `html` formatter should emit a standalone report showing old and new references and allowing include/exclude filtering over displayed file paths. If no matching reference can be found for a reference-only side, raise a user-facing `ConanException` instead of silently succeeding.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run a single report command to compare two Conan recipes by version, revision, or local working copy and see what changed in the recipe and related source material. The comparison should work whether the inputs come from cache, remotes, or local recipe files, automatically picking the newest revision when the user omits one. The result should be available as raw diff text, structured JSON for tooling, or an HTML report that is easy to browse and filter by file path. Missing references should fail clearly instead of producing an empty or misleading report.

constraints.grounded: Reference-only comparisons must continue to search the local cache before or alongside the enabled remotes, and remote downloads should only occur when the selected reference is not already local. Supplying `--old-path` or `--new-path` must not require the referenced revision to exist remotely, and the path-based side must use the supplied reference only as the comparison identity. If the user omits a revision in a reference, the command must not force manual revision selection when a latest recipe revision can be resolved. HTML output must be emitted as report content only and remain usable without any automatic file opening behavior. Output formatting must preserve per-file diff information rather than collapsing the result into a summary.
constraints.conceptual: The new diff feature should stay compatible with existing Conan reference lookup behavior, work without extra revision bookkeeping when Conan can determine the latest revision itself, and let local recipe directories participate in the comparison without first publishing them. The report should remain a content-producing command rather than launching external viewers, and each output format should retain enough detail for users to inspect file-level changes.

behavior: A new `conan report diff` command compares two recipe inputs and includes recipe-related source material in the diff result, not just a high-level metadata summary.
Each comparison side can be provided either as a reference alone or as a local recipe path paired with a reference.
For reference-only inputs, Conan searches local cache and enabled remotes; if the reference omits a recipe revision, Conan resolves the latest available recipe revision automatically.
For local-path inputs, Conan exports the local recipe under the provided reference identity and uses that exported content in the comparison.
The command accepts repeated `--remote` values to limit or define which remotes are considered for reference resolution and download.
`text` output returns the raw diff, `json` output returns a structured diff grouped by file, and `html` output returns a standalone rendered diff report.
The HTML report shows the old and new references and supports include and exclude path filtering over the visible file list and diff sections.
If a reference-only input cannot be resolved from cache or the selected remotes, the command raises a user-facing error instead of emitting a partial report.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan report diff` with two valid recipe references, it should produce a diff of the compared recipes and their associated configured source content in the selected output format.

When either reference omits a recipe revision and a latest recipe revision is available in cache or the enabled remotes, the command should resolve that latest revision automatically and use it for the comparison.

When a user supplies `--old-path` or `--new-path` together with its companion reference, the command should compare that local recipe content against the other side without requiring the local side to exist as an already-resolved remote revision.

When the user selects `-f text`, the output should be a raw diff; when the user selects `-f json`, the output should be machine-readable and grouped by file; when the user selects `-f html`, the output should be a standalone HTML report that labels old and new inputs and supports path-based include/exclude filtering.

When a reference-only side cannot be found in the local cache or enabled remotes, the command should fail with a clear Conan error indicating that no matching reference was found and that a local path can be provided for comparison instead.
When HTML output is generated, Conan should emit the report content for the user to save or open explicitly, rather than automatically launching it.

task_19.title: Add PremakeToolchain-based premake5 integration
task_19.description: Conan 2.18.0 adds a dedicated Premake toolchain workflow for premake5 and expands the Premake helper so Conan can drive configuration and builds with mapped architectures, Conan-managed flags, dependency setup, and platform-specific defaults. The change makes Premake a first-class integrated build flow rather than only a dependency generator.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that premake5-based Conan consumers can use a Conan-generated Premake toolchain so dependency setup, compiler and linker settings, architecture selection, and build execution are integrated consistently across supported platforms and project layouts.

expectation.grounded: Expose `PremakeToolchain` as a public generator in `conan.tools.premake` and support using it together with `PremakeDeps` and `Premake`. `PremakeToolchain` should generate a premake5 toolchain entrypoint that can include Conan dependency setup, apply Conan workspace defaults, translate Conan `compiler.cppstd` and `compiler.cstd` into Premake dialect settings, propagate Conan-controlled `shared` and `fPIC` defaults where applicable, honor `tools.build:cflags`, `tools.build:cxxflags`, `tools.build:sharedlinkflags`, `tools.build:exelinkflags`, `tools.build:defines`, and toolchain extra flag lists, and include architecture-, threading-, and libc++-related flags and definitions. When `tools.build:compiler_executables` defines `c` or `cpp`, the generated Premake build environment should expose the corresponding compiler executables. `Premake.configure()` should use the generated toolchain when present, invoke premake5 with a Premake-compatible architecture mapping, and honor `tools.build:verbosity`. `Premake.build()` should require `PremakeToolchain`, build Visual Studio actions through `MSBuild` and non-MSVC actions through `make`, and honor `tools.build:jobs` and `tools.compilation:verbosity`. `PremakeDeps` should generate configuration-specific dependency metadata keyed by Premake-style architecture names so dependency resolution matches the selected Premake platform.
expectation.conceptual: Using Premake with Conan should become a complete premake5 workflow: Conan should generate the build setup consumed by Premake, carry dependency and compiler settings into the generated project files, choose the correct platform and architecture representation, and run the appropriate backend build command with consistent verbosity and parallelism behavior.

constraints.grounded: Preserve `Premake.configure()` compatibility when no `PremakeToolchain` file exists, but require `PremakeToolchain` for `Premake.build()`. Do not override a project `kind` that is already explicitly set; only apply Conan-controlled shared or static defaults to projects that leave `kind` unset. Keep project-specific overrides additive to workspace-level settings. Reject Conan architectures that do not map to a supported Premake architecture instead of generating an invalid premake invocation. Keep the integration scoped to premake5.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should not silently break existing configure-only flows, should fail clearly for unsupported architectures instead of producing unusable build files, and should respect explicit project-level build choices while still allowing Conan to supply defaults and shared configuration.

behavior: `PremakeToolchain` is available as a Conan generator and public import for premake5 workflows.
