The generated Premake toolchain can apply Conan workspace settings such as output directories, language standard settings, shared or static library defaults, position-independent code, Conan dependency setup, compiler and linker flags, preprocessor definitions, and compiler executable mappings derived from Conan configuration and toolchain extras.

`PremakeToolchain.project(name)` supports project-specific overrides, including extra compile flags, extra link flags, extra definitions, explicit project kind, and disabling a named project from normal build output.
`Premake.configure()` now prefers a Conan-managed Lua entrypoint plus Premake architecture mapping when the toolchain is present, and non-MSVC Premake generation defaults to the `gmake` action.

`Premake.build(workspace, targets=None)` is added to execute the generated build through `MSBuild` for Visual Studio actions or `make` for other actions, using Conan-controlled job count and verbosity.

Premake architecture selection now normalizes Conan architectures to Premake architecture names, including ARM, ARM64, E2K, RISC-V, wasm32, and wasm64 variants, and unsupported architectures raise a Conan exception during configure.
`PremakeDeps` now keys configuration-specific dependency data by Premake-style configuration and architecture names so dependency selection aligns with the resolved Premake platform.
Conan's premake project scaffolding now includes library and application templates that use `PremakeDeps`, `PremakeToolchain`, and `Premake` together.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe declares `PremakeToolchain`, Conan install should emit a premake5 toolchain configuration that applies Conan dependency setup and Conan-derived workspace settings to the generated Premake build files.

When a recipe combines `PremakeToolchain` with `Premake.configure()`, Premake should be invoked through a Conan-managed entrypoint and receive the Premake architecture corresponding to the active Conan architecture.

When `PremakeToolchain.project("name")` is used, only the named project should receive the declared project-level overrides or disabling behavior, while workspace-level settings remain available to the rest of the workspace.

When Conan controls `shared` for a library project and the Premake project does not explicitly set `kind`, the generated configuration should select the matching shared or static library kind; if `kind` is already explicit, Conan should not replace it.
When `tools.build:compiler_executables` provides `c` or `cpp`, the Premake workflow should use those compiler executables through the generated Conan build environment.
When `Premake.build()` is called after toolchain generation, it should build through `MSBuild` for Visual Studio actions or `make` for non-MSVC actions, honoring Conan job and verbosity settings.
When the active Conan architecture has no supported Premake mapping, configuration should fail with a Conan exception instead of generating an invalid Premake invocation.

When `PremakeDeps` and `PremakeToolchain` are used together on mapped architectures such as ARM64 or WebAssembly, dependency configuration selection should follow the normalized Premake architecture name rather than the raw Conan architecture string.

When platform-specific defaults apply, the generated toolchain should expose the expected Premake behavior for those targets, including macOS runtime loader-path handling and Emscripten application output handling.

task_21.title: Handle absolute -of paths correctly in generators
task_21.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes generator path handling so installs that use an absolute `-of` output folder no longer produce incorrect absolute paths in generated metadata. Equivalent paths are now matched consistently across slash styles, preserving the intended relative layout in generator outputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running `conan install` with an absolute `-of` output folder does not cause generators to emit incorrect absolute filesystem paths where paths relative to the generated output should be produced.

expectation.grounded: When `conan install` is executed with `-of` set to an absolute output folder, generator path relativization must still recognize paths under the shared generators/output base and emit paths relative to the generators folder instead of leaving those paths as absolute filesystem locations. This comparison must remain correct even when equivalent paths use different path separators.
expectation.conceptual: Using an absolute install output directory should behave the same as using an equivalent relative output directory from the perspective of generated files. Generator metadata should keep referring to installed content through the intended relative layout rather than baking in incorrect machine-specific absolute paths.

constraints.grounded: Do not change behavior for empty paths or for paths that are outside the common generators/output base; those values should continue to pass through unchanged. Preserve normalized forward-slash style in relativized generator paths, and limit the fix to incorrect mismatches caused by separator-format differences in equivalent absolute paths.
constraints.conceptual: Only correct false path mismatches for the same location. Do not rewrite unrelated external paths or alter valid generator output structure beyond making absolute-output installs resolve paths correctly.

behavior: Generators that rely on path relativization now treat equivalent absolute paths as the same common base even when the compared paths use different slash conventions.
For paths inside the install output and generators tree, generated metadata now keeps the intended relative references instead of incorrectly retaining absolute filesystem paths.
Paths that are empty or outside the shared output base continue to remain unchanged rather than being forcibly relativized.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan install` is run with `-of` pointing to an absolute directory, generated dependency or configuration files should reference installed package content using the same relative layout that would be produced for an equivalent relative output folder.
When generator path comparison involves equivalent locations expressed with different path separators, the generated files should still resolve them as the same base and emit valid relative paths.
When a path lies outside the generators/output base, the generator should preserve that path instead of converting it to a relative output-based reference.

task_22.title: Clarify invalid cpp_info.requires component references
task_22.description: The upgrade improves diagnostics for invalid `cpp_info.requires` declarations. Package-qualified component requirements with extra `::` segments are now interpreted in a way that preserves the dependency name and reports a missing component against that dependency, giving users an actionable resolution error instead of an opaque parsing failure.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that incorrectly defined `cpp_info.requires` entries produce a clear dependency and component resolution error, including when a requirement string contains more than one `::` separator.

expectation.grounded: When Conan processes `cpp_info.requires`, package-qualified entries should be split at the first `::` only. If a value such as `pkg::comp::extra` refers to an existing package requirement but a non-existent component name, Conan should fail with a component-not-found diagnostic for that package using the original qualified reference rather than misparsing the value.
expectation.conceptual: Users who declare an invalid component dependency should receive an actionable error that identifies the wrong component and the dependency it belongs to, even if the declaration includes extra scope separators.

constraints.grounded: Valid `cpp_info.requires` forms must keep their current behavior: unqualified component names remain local component requirements, and well-formed `pkg::component` references continue to resolve normally. The parser must not split beyond the first package and component separator.
constraints.conceptual: Correct dependency declarations should behave exactly as before. The change should only improve diagnostics for invalid declarations and should not alter how valid requirements are resolved.

behavior: `cpp_info.requires` entries containing `::` are interpreted as a package reference plus a component reference, split only at the first separator.
A reference with extra `::` segments is validated as a component lookup within the named package requirement instead of failing during parsing.
If the package requirement exists but the referenced component does not, Conan reports a targeted missing-component error for that dependency.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe defines `cpp_info.requires` with an entry like `pkg::comp::extra` and `pkg` is a valid requirement, Conan should fail with an error indicating that the referenced component cannot be found in `pkg`.
When `cpp_info.requires` contains a valid `pkg::component` entry, Conan should continue resolving it without changing existing behavior.
When `cpp_info.requires` contains a component name without `::`, Conan should continue treating it as an unqualified component requirement.

task_23.title: PowerShell-safe MSBuild verbosity for CMake Visual Studio builds
task_23.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes a Windows PowerShell compatibility issue in CMake Visual Studio builds. When MSBuild verbosity is configured and the PowerShell virtualenv setting is enabled, Conan now emits an equivalent verbosity switch format that survives PowerShell argument handling so the requested verbosity level is preserved and the build does not fail on malformed MSBuild arguments.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Visual Studio CMake builds launched through the PowerShell virtualenv configuration preserve the configured MSBuild verbosity setting without causing the downstream build tool to misparse the verbosity argument and fail.

expectation.grounded: When `conan.tools.cmake.CMake.build()` is used with a Visual Studio generator and a configured MSBuild verbosity setting, enabling `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` should make Conan pass the MSBuild verbosity option in the slash-prefixed form accepted by MSBuild instead of the hyphen-prefixed form. The selected verbosity level must still be forwarded through CMake's build-tool arguments as one effective option and must no longer trigger MSBuild argument parsing failures caused by PowerShell splitting `-name:value` tokens after `--`.
expectation.conceptual: PowerShell-based CMake builds for Visual Studio should honor user-selected build verbosity without breaking command-line parsing. Users who enable PowerShell virtual environments should get the same effective MSBuild verbosity behavior as before, but in a command format that is compatible with PowerShell.

constraints.grounded: Apply this compatibility adjustment only when a Visual Studio generator produces an MSBuild verbosity argument and `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` is enabled. Do not alter behavior for non-Visual Studio generators, builds with no verbosity setting, or executions that are not using the PowerShell virtualenv configuration.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to the PowerShell and Visual Studio verbosity case and must not change unrelated CMake argument handling or other build configurations.

behavior: For Visual Studio generators, Conan continues to derive an MSBuild verbosity command-line option from the user's configured build verbosity.

When `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` is enabled, Conan reformats that MSBuild verbosity option from hyphen-prefixed syntax to the equivalent slash-prefixed syntax before forwarding it through CMake build-tool arguments.
The requested verbosity level remains the same after reformatting, but the resulting command line is compatible with PowerShell's handling of arguments that appear after `--`.
When the PowerShell virtualenv configuration is not enabled, Conan preserves the existing verbosity argument format.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `CMake.build()` with a Visual Studio generator, configures build verbosity, and enables `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell`, the generated build invocation should pass the MSBuild verbosity switch in slash-prefixed form and the build should not fail because the verbosity argument was split or misparsed by PowerShell.
When the same Visual Studio build uses configured verbosity without the PowerShell virtualenv setting, Conan should keep the existing verbosity argument style.
When no build verbosity is configured, enabling the PowerShell virtualenv setting should not add any extra MSBuild verbosity switch.
When the generator is not a Visual Studio generator, this PowerShell-specific compatibility behavior should not change the generated build-tool arguments.

task_24.title: Improve artifact-scoped cache integrity output
task_24.description: Version 2.18.0 improves the user-facing output of `conan cache check-integrity` so each result is clearly tied to the exact cached recipe or package being checked, and manifest corruption is reported as a readable summary that includes the affected folder and per-file differences.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache check-integrity` clearly identifies the exact cached recipe or package artifact being checked and presents missing-manifest and manifest-mismatch failures in a consolidated, readable form.

expectation.grounded: `conan cache check-integrity` should report recipe and package results against the current `RecipeReference` or `PkgReference` rendered with `repr_notime()`. Successful checks should emit the status `Integrity check: ok`. If recipe or package manifests cannot be loaded, the command should report `Manifest missing` for that scoped artifact. If the stored and computed manifests differ, the command should emit one grouped manifest-mismatch error for that artifact containing a mismatch heading, the affected folder, and one entry per differing file showing both manifest and current file digests.
expectation.conceptual: Running the cache integrity command should tell users exactly which cached artifact each success or failure belongs to, and corruption reports should be grouped into a clear summary that explains whether the manifest is missing or which files differ from the manifest.

constraints.grounded: The update must preserve the existing integrity-check decision logic for both recipes and packages; it changes how results are presented, not which artifacts are considered valid or corrupted. The same reporting structure should apply to recipe-level and package-level checks.
constraints.conceptual: Improve clarity of the integrity report without changing the underlying corruption detection behavior, and keep the reporting consistent across recipes and packages.

behavior: Successful recipe and package integrity checks are reported against the exact artifact reference being examined and use the normalized success status `Integrity check: ok`.
If a recipe or package manifest file is missing, the command reports a `Manifest missing` error for that specific artifact.

If a recipe or package manifest does not match the current cache contents, the command reports a single grouped `Manifest mismatch` error for that specific artifact instead of splitting the summary across separate error lines.

A manifest-mismatch report includes the affected artifact folder and one line per differing file, with both the manifest digest and the current file digest/value shown so missing, added, or changed files are visible in the report.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan cache check-integrity` checks a valid cached recipe, it should report success for that recipe using the exact artifact reference and the status `Integrity check: ok`.
When `conan cache check-integrity` checks a valid cached package, it should report success for that package using the exact artifact reference and the status `Integrity check: ok`.
When a checked recipe or package is missing its manifest, the command should report `Manifest missing` for that artifact rather than an unscoped or ambiguous error.

When a checked recipe or package has manifest/content differences, the command should emit a single readable corruption summary for that artifact that includes the mismatch heading, the artifact folder, and the differing files with manifest-versus-current values.
When multiple artifacts are checked in one command, each success or failure should remain attributable to the specific artifact it belongs to.

task_25.title: Fail fast on invalid conf_info definitions
task_25.description: The 2.18.0 update tightens `conf_info` validation so malformed or unknown configuration entries defined by packages are rejected during `package_info()` instead of being accepted or reported ambiguously. It also distinguishes invalid `user` configuration syntax from unknown built-in or tool configuration keys so package metadata failures are clearer at runtime.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that packages cannot publish invalid `conf_info` entries. Invalid configuration keys defined through `conf_info` should fail during package evaluation, and malformed `user` configuration names should be reported as format errors rather than generic unknown-configuration errors.

expectation.grounded: After `package_info()` populates `conanfile.conf_info`, Conan should validate the resulting entries and raise `ConanException` if any item uses an invalid configuration name. Entries in the `user` namespace must follow the `user.org.group:conf` format, while non-`user` entries must match a known configuration key; failures should surface as an error attributed to `package_info()`.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading to 2.18.0 should make malformed package configuration metadata fail immediately and clearly. Custom `user` configuration keys need the documented namespace format, and unsupported configuration keys should be rejected as unknown instead of being treated as vaguely invalid.

constraints.grounded: Valid `conf_info` entries must continue to work unchanged. The change should only reject malformed `user` keys and unknown configuration names, and it should report them as runtime validation errors during package metadata evaluation rather than silently accepting them.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change the behavior of correctly defined configuration metadata. Only tighten validation for bad keys, and keep the failure scoped to cases where a package exposes invalid configuration information.

behavior: `conf_info` entries are now validated after `package_info()` runs, and invalid entries raise `ConanException` instead of remaining unchecked.
Malformed `user` configuration names are identified specifically as invalid `user` conf definitions when they do not follow the required `user.org.group:conf` structure.
Unknown non-`user` configuration names are rejected as unknown configuration keys with a clearer error classification instead of a combined unknown-or-invalid-format error.
acceptance_criteria: When a package defines an invalid `conf_info` key in `package_info()`, Conan should stop processing that package and raise a `ConanException` from the `package_info()` context.
When the invalid `conf_info` key is a `user` configuration name that does not follow `user.org.group:conf`, Conan should report it as a user configuration format error.
When the invalid `conf_info` key is not in the `user` namespace and is not a recognized configuration key, Conan should report it as an unknown configuration entry.
When `conf_info` contains only recognized configuration keys and correctly formatted `user` keys, this validation should not introduce a new failure.

task_26.title: Recognize QCC C++20 support on QNX 8.0
task_26.description: Conan 2.18.0 updates qcc compiler standard detection so modern QNX 8.0 toolchains are treated as supporting C++20 and GNU C++20, preventing Conan from incorrectly capping those environments at C++17.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recognizes modern `qcc` toolchains used with QNX 8.0 as supporting `compiler.cppstd=20` and `compiler.cppstd=gnu20`, instead of incorrectly treating them as limited to C++17.

expectation.grounded: For `qcc`, `conan.tools.build.supported_cppstd()` must report `20` and `gnu20` as supported values when `compiler.version` is `12` or newer. Existing behavior must remain for older `qcc` versions: versions below `5` support only `98` and `gnu98`, while versions from `5` up to but not including `12` support `98`/`gnu98`, `11`/`gnu11`, `14`/`gnu14`, and `17`/`gnu17`. Conan behaviors that rely on the supported `cppstd` list, including `compiler.cppstd` validation and `conan.tools.build` C++ standard compatibility checks, must therefore treat `20` and `gnu20` as valid only for `qcc` 12+.
expectation.conceptual: Users targeting QNX 8.0 with a recent `qcc` compiler should be able to request C++20 in Conan and have it recognized as a supported configuration. Older `qcc` toolchains should keep their previous limits so unsupported standards are still rejected.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter supported `cppstd` detection for compilers other than `qcc`. For `qcc`, preserve the existing supported-standard ranges for versions earlier than `12`; the only new supported values introduced by this change are `20` and `gnu20` for `qcc` version `12` and newer.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be narrowly scoped to the affected `qcc` capability mapping. It must not expand C++20 support for unrelated compilers or for older `qcc` toolchains that do not support it.

behavior: When Conan resolves supported C++ standards for `qcc` version `12` or newer, the returned set now includes `20` and `gnu20` in addition to the previously supported standards up to `17`/`gnu17`.
When Conan resolves supported C++ standards for `qcc` versions from `5` up to but not including `12`, the supported set remains capped at `17` and `gnu17`.
When Conan resolves supported C++ standards for `qcc` versions below `5`, the supported set remains limited to `98` and `gnu98`.
Any user-visible Conan validation or compatibility logic that depends on the supported `cppstd` list now accepts C++20 selections for `qcc` 12+ and continues to reject them for older `qcc` versions.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan profile or recipe uses `compiler=qcc` with `compiler.version` `12` or newer, Conan should recognize `compiler.cppstd=20` as supported.
When a Conan profile or recipe uses `compiler=qcc` with `compiler.version` `12` or newer, Conan should recognize `compiler.cppstd=gnu20` as supported.

When a Conan profile or recipe uses `compiler=qcc` with a version from `5` up to but not including `12`, Conan should continue to allow standards only up to `17` and `gnu17`, and should not treat `20` or `gnu20` as supported.
When a Conan profile or recipe uses `compiler=qcc` with a version below `5`, Conan should continue to allow only `98` and `gnu98`.

task_27.title: Fix CycloneDX component bom-ref generation for special root graphs
task_27.description: CycloneDX SBOM exports should keep each component's bom-ref tied to the Conan package identity even when the dependency graph includes a synthetic root node, so downstream SBOM consumers receive correct component references in 1.4 and 1.6 outputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CycloneDX SBOM generation assigns each component a package-derived bom-ref even when the dependency graph includes a synthetic root node, so exported SBOMs expose correct component identities to downstream consumers.

expectation.grounded: The CycloneDX SBOM generators for versions 1.4 and 1.6 should emit each component's `bom-ref` from the Conan package identity, including package name, version, and recipe revision, regardless of whether the graph contains a synthetic root node. This change applies to the component entries in the generated SBOM payload and preserves the existing package-based bom-ref behavior for normal graphs.
expectation.conceptual: CycloneDX exports should always identify components by their real Conan package identity. A synthetic project root must not replace the component reference that external SBOM tooling uses to recognize the package.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the supported CycloneDX output versions or unrelated component metadata. The fix is limited to preventing synthetic-root handling from substituting a non-package identifier for a component's package-derived `bom-ref`, while keeping the established package-based format for ordinary graphs.
constraints.conceptual: Only correct how component references are chosen. The update must not otherwise change which SBOM components are emitted or alter unrelated SBOM fields.

behavior: CycloneDX 1.4 SBOM generation now keeps component `bom-ref` values package-derived even when the dependency graph contains a synthetic root node.
CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM generation now keeps component `bom-ref` values package-derived even when the dependency graph contains a synthetic root node.
Graphs without a synthetic root node continue to emit the same package-based component `bom-ref` style as before.
acceptance_criteria: When generating a CycloneDX 1.4 SBOM for a graph with a synthetic root node, each component `bom-ref` should identify the Conan package itself rather than the synthetic root.
When generating a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM for a graph with a synthetic root node, each component `bom-ref` should identify the Conan package itself rather than the synthetic root.
When generating a CycloneDX SBOM for a graph without a synthetic root node, component `bom-ref` values should continue to use the established package-based identity format.

task_28.title: Deprecate Node.dependencies in favor of Node.edges
task_28.description: Conan 2.18.0 renames a graph node's outbound dependency collection from `Node.dependencies` to `Node.edges`, updates built-in graph consumers to use the new name, and keeps the old attribute as a deprecated compatibility alias so older integrations continue to run while they migrate.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that graph-inspection integrations move from `Node.dependencies` to `Node.edges`, while legacy reads from `Node.dependencies` remain temporarily functional and clearly deprecated during the 2.18.0 upgrade.

expectation.grounded: In Conan 2.18.0, `conan.internal.graph.graph.Node` must use `Node.edges` as the canonical ordered collection of outbound dependency edges. Accessing `Node.dependencies` must still succeed as a compatibility alias that returns the same ordered edge collection, but it must emit a deprecation warning indicating that callers should migrate to `Node.edges` and that the old name will be removed in a future version. Reads that inspect edge existence, iterate outgoing edges, or access destinations such as the first edge's `dst` must observe the same results through `Node.edges` as they previously did through `Node.dependencies`.
expectation.conceptual: The dependency graph model should expose outbound links under `Node.edges`. Older code that still reads `Node.dependencies` should keep working in 2.18.0, but it should receive a clear deprecation warning so consumers know they need to migrate before the alias disappears.

constraints.grounded: The deprecated alias must remain read-compatible in 2.18.0: it should preserve ordering, expose the same edge objects as `Node.edges`, and avoid introducing a new hard failure for existing `Node.dependencies` readers. Renaming the attribute must not change graph traversal outcomes or other runtime decisions that depend on whether a node has outbound edges and which destinations those edges reference.
constraints.conceptual: This rename should be backward compatible for existing consumers in the current release. The only new observable effect for legacy usage should be a deprecation signal, not a change in dependency graph results.

behavior: `Node.edges` becomes the canonical ordered collection of a node's outbound dependency edges.
Reading `Node.dependencies` continues to return the same outbound edge collection exposed by `Node.edges`.
Each access to `Node.dependencies` emits a deprecation warning telling consumers to migrate to `Node.edges` before the old attribute is removed.
Operations that rely on outbound edge presence, iteration order, or destination lookup observe the same results after migrating from `Node.dependencies` to `Node.edges`.
acceptance_criteria: When a graph node has outbound dependencies, reading `node.edges` should return them in their existing order.
When existing automation reads `node.dependencies`, it should still receive the same outbound edges as `node.edges` and a deprecation warning should be emitted.
When callers inspect destinations through the outbound edge list, migrating from `node.dependencies` to `node.edges` should preserve the same destination objects and ordering.
When a node has no outbound dependencies, `node.edges` should be empty and `node.dependencies` should behave equivalently apart from the deprecation warning.

task_30.title: Fix Git remote URL parsing for tree-less repositories
task_30.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes `Git.get_remote_url()` so it returns the actual repository URL for tree-less Git remotes instead of leaving Git transport annotations in the result. The update also preserves valid local repository paths that may contain spaces or parentheses while keeping Windows local path normalization behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `Git.get_remote_url()` returns only the configured repository URL for tree-less Git repositories and does not expose Git remote direction annotations in the value returned to users.

expectation.grounded: `conan.tools.scm.Git.get_remote_url()` should parse the selected remote from `git remote -v` output and return only the remote URL, even when Git appends tree-less clone metadata and a trailing `(fetch)` or `(push)` marker. After cleanup, if the resolved URL points to an existing local directory on Windows, it should continue to be normalized to forward slashes before being returned.
expectation.conceptual: When users request a Git remote URL through Conan, they should receive the real repository location, not extra text added by Git for tree-less clones or remote direction labels. Local repository paths should continue to work even if they contain spaces or parentheses.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress `Git.get_remote_url()` for ordinary remotes that already return a clean URL. Preserve support for local repository URLs containing whitespace, and do not treat parentheses inside a valid local path as removable metadata. Keep the method behavior limited to returning the parsed URL string for the requested remote.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only remove Git-added annotations and must not corrupt valid remote locations. Existing remote URL handling should remain stable, including for local paths with spaces or parentheses.

behavior: `Git.get_remote_url()` removes a trailing `(fetch)` or `(push)` token if it remains after parsing the selected remote entry.
Tree-less remote output is reduced to the repository URL instead of returning a URL string that still includes Git transport annotations.
Local repository paths that contain spaces remain supported because URL parsing continues to trim only trailing metadata tokens.
If the resolved remote URL is an existing Windows local directory, the returned value still uses forward slashes.
acceptance_criteria: When the configured remote is reported by Git with tree-less clone metadata and a trailing `(fetch)` marker, `Git.get_remote_url()` should return only the repository URL.
When the configured remote is reported by Git with tree-less clone metadata and a trailing `(push)` marker, `Git.get_remote_url()` should return only the repository URL.
When the remote URL is a valid local path containing spaces, `Git.get_remote_url()` should return the full path without truncating it at the first whitespace.
When the remote URL is a valid local path containing parentheses, `Git.get_remote_url()` should preserve those parentheses as part of the returned path.
When the resolved remote points to an existing Windows local directory, `Git.get_remote_url()` should return the normalized path using forward slashes.

task_32.title: Normalize Windows CMake preset include paths
task_32.description: The update fixes Conan-generated CMake presets on Windows by making relative preset include paths portable. User preset files should reference included preset files with normalized separators so the include is preserved in shared-folder and cross-platform workflows.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan-generated CMake user presets remain valid on Windows by writing portable include paths for referenced preset files.

expectation.grounded: When `CMakeToolchain` generates `CMakeUserPresets.json` and includes another preset through a relative path, the value written to the `include` array should use `/` separators even on Windows. The referenced preset should remain included and usable instead of being lost because the path contains Windows-style backslashes.
expectation.conceptual: Generated CMake user presets should use portable include paths so preset chaining works reliably for Windows users, including workflows where the presets are consumed from shared folders or by non-Windows tooling.

constraints.grounded: Only the formatting of relative included preset paths should change. Relative includes should remain relative, absolute-path handling should continue to behave as before, and no new warnings or errors should be introduced for otherwise valid preset generation.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve path portability without changing which preset file is referenced or altering unrelated preset-generation behavior.

behavior: When Conan computes a relative preset include path for `CMakeUserPresets.json`, Windows path separators in that include value are normalized to forward slashes before the file is written.
The generated `include` entry becomes portable across environments that do not reliably preserve backslash-based preset paths.
Preset generation behavior outside of this relative include path normalization remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a Windows user generates `CMakeUserPresets.json` with `CMakeToolchain` and the file includes another preset by relative path, the `include` entry should contain `/` separators and should not contain `\` separators.

When the generated preset file is consumed in a shared-folder or cross-platform workflow, the referenced Conan preset should remain included instead of being ignored because of Windows path separators.
When preset generation uses paths that are not subject to relative-path rewriting, the referenced preset location and overall inclusion behavior should remain unchanged.

task_31.title: Normalize mixed-visibility dependency graph convergence
task_31.description: Conan 2.18.0 improves dependency graph resolution when the same dependency is reached with different visibility settings. Real dependency mismatches are now surfaced as normal graph conflicts, while compatible resolutions are preserved with a warning and a cleaned-up graph instead of leaving malformed or orphaned nodes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency graphs remain well-formed when the same package is required through both `visible=True` and `visible=False` paths. Ensure that incompatible resolutions still fail as a normal dependency conflict, and that compatible resolutions keep a single clean graph while warning users that mixed visibility was detected.

expectation.grounded: When downstream propagation encounters the same dependency reference through requirements whose `visible` values differ, Conan should treat different resolved package references as a standard graph conflict. When the converging requirements resolve to the same package reference, the dependency graph should record the mixed-visibility condition, print a graph warning identifying the affected reference and consumer references, aggregate the requirement state, reconcile direct dependency edges, and remove unreachable orphan nodes from the final graph.
expectation.conceptual: If a package is pulled into the graph once as visible and once as hidden, Conan should no longer produce a malformed graph. A real version mismatch should be reported as the same kind of dependency conflict users see elsewhere. If the dependency can be unified to one resolved package, the command should succeed, warn about the mixed visibility, and show only the normalized dependency graph.

constraints.grounded: Do not downgrade genuine resolved-reference mismatches to warnings; incompatible resolutions must still stop graph resolution as a conflict. Only emit the mixed-visibility warning when the same dependency is converging with different visibility values in a direct-dependency context. After reconciliation, the final graph must not retain stale edges or nodes that are no longer reachable from the graph root.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve real dependency conflict detection, avoid introducing warnings for normal graphs, and leave users with a clean final graph that contains only dependencies that still participate in the resolved topology.

behavior: Converging requirements for the same dependency that resolve to different package references now fail as a standard graph conflict instead of a separate runtime-conflict path.
Converging requirements for the same dependency that differ by `visible=True` versus `visible=False` are tracked as a visibility issue when they unify to the same resolved package reference.
Graph-related CLI output warns when a package was required with both visibility settings and identifies the affected dependency and the consuming package or packages.
When mixed-visibility requirements are unified, direct dependency edges are reconciled so only the surviving direct nodes remain attached to the consumer.
After visibility reconciliation, unreachable orphan nodes are removed so exported graph representations reflect only reachable dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: When the same dependency is reached through visible and hidden paths and those paths resolve to different package references, graph resolution should fail with a normal dependency conflict that identifies the conflicting dependency origin.

When the same dependency is reached through visible and hidden paths but both paths resolve to one package reference, graph resolution should succeed and emit a warning that the dependency was required with both visibility settings.

When mixed visibility is resolved without a conflict, the final graph output should contain only reachable nodes for the normalized dependency structure and should not keep detached orphan package entries.
When a graph does not contain a mixed-visibility convergence for the same dependency, the mixed-visibility warning should not be emitted.

task_29.title: Graceful errors for broken local-recipes-index remotes
task_29.description: Conan 2.18.0 improves local-recipes-index remote handling for version-range lookups and other recipe searches. If the local repository layout is incomplete, the client now reports a clear remote connection failure instead of leaking an internal filesystem exception, and non-exact search patterns are broadened so local version discovery can proceed against available package versions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that operations using a local-recipes-index remote, especially version-range resolution, fail predictably when the repository layout is incomplete by showing a clear user-facing remote error instead of an internal stack trace, while still allowing non-exact lookups to discover available versions for the requested package.

expectation.grounded: When RemoteManager routes a call to a local-recipes-index client and _LocalRecipesIndexLayout.get_recipes_references() finds that the repository lacks its required recipes directory, the local client should raise a connection-style failure that is surfaced as a ConanConnectionError for that remote rather than leaking a raw filesystem exception. If the search pattern cannot be parsed as an exact RecipeReference, recipe enumeration should fall back to scanning all versions under the matched package name so version-range requests can obtain local candidates.
expectation.conceptual: Commands that consult a local recipes index, including installs that use version ranges, should either inspect the package versions available in that index or fail with a clear remote-access error explaining that the local repository is missing its recipes area. Users should not see an unhandled stack trace for this condition.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing behavior unchanged for disabled remotes, normal remote calls, and valid local-recipes-index repositories. Only the missing recipes directory case should be translated into the standard remote connection error flow for local folder remotes, and exact recipe reference searches that already parse successfully should continue using their specific name/version filter.
constraints.conceptual: Do not alter normal behavior for healthy remotes or exact package lookups. Limit the change to making broken local index layouts report cleanly and ensuring non-exact local searches still consider the requested package's available versions.

behavior: A local-recipes-index search now detects when the repository has no recipes directory and reports that missing folder as a connection failure.

Connection failures raised while calling a local folder remote now go through the same remote error handling as other remotes and are surfaced as a ConanConnectionError with remote context instead of an uncaught filesystem exception.

When a local-recipes-index search pattern is not a parseable exact recipe reference, candidate discovery falls back to all versions of the matched package name instead of applying the raw non-exact pattern directly as the initial fnmatch filter.
acceptance_criteria: When a command resolves a version range through a configured local-recipes-index remote whose repository layout lacks the required recipes directory, it should fail with a clear remote connection error indicating that the local index is missing its recipes folder.
When that failure originates from a local folder remote, the reported error should preserve remote context and should not expose a raw filesystem exception or internal stack trace.

When a valid local-recipes-index remote is queried with a version-range or other non-exact package pattern, it should consider the available versions for the requested package name so local candidate discovery can proceed.

task_33.title: Reduce verbosity in default conan upload output
task_33.description: Conan 2.18.0 makes the default text output of `conan upload` less verbose by omitting upload URL metadata from routine CLI summaries while preserving the visible upload result for each item.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the default human-readable output of `conan upload` stays concise by hiding upload URL metadata from routine upload summaries while still clearly showing whether each item was uploaded or skipped.

expectation.grounded: When `conan upload` renders its basic text summary, result entries must not expose the `upload-urls` field. The command should continue to present the normal per-entry upload outcome in the text output, and only the extra upload URL metadata should be suppressed.
expectation.conceptual: Users running `conan upload` in the standard CLI format should see a compact status-oriented summary, not low-level transport details about where individual files would be uploaded.

constraints.grounded: Do not change which artifacts are considered uploaded or skipped, and do not remove the visible upload status from the basic text output. Limit the change to suppressing upload URL metadata from the routine text summary.
constraints.conceptual: Make the CLI quieter without changing upload behavior or hiding the status information users rely on to understand the outcome.

behavior: The default text summary produced by `conan upload` no longer displays upload URL metadata when that metadata is present in the upload results.
Per-item upload outcomes remain visible in the human-readable summary so users can still tell whether content was uploaded or skipped.
Nested transport details that are only surfaced through upload URL metadata are omitted from the routine text output.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan upload` with the default text output and the underlying result contains upload URL metadata, the printed summary should not include an `upload-urls` section.
When the basic text summary is shown, it should still clearly report the upload outcome for each listed item.
When upload URL metadata exists for files or revisions, routine CLI output should remain concise and should not print those transport details.

task_34.title: Create Missing Folders for `--out-file`
task_34.description: The CLI now creates missing parent directories automatically when command output is redirected with `--out-file`, so users can target nested file paths without manually preparing the directory structure first.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that commands using `--out-file` can write output to files inside directories that do not yet exist by automatically creating the required parent folders.

expectation.grounded: When a Conan CLI command is invoked with `--out-file` and the target path includes a parent directory that does not exist, the CLI must create that directory path before opening the file and redirecting command output. This should cover nested relative paths, including paths that traverse to a parent directory, and should prevent failures caused only by a missing destination folder.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to send command output to a file in a new folder with `--out-file` without creating folders manually first. The command should succeed and place the output in the requested file.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter `--out-file` behavior for targets that have no directory component. Existing destination directories must continue to work without error, and the change must preserve normal output redirection to the specified file.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should remove the need to pre-create folders, but it must not change the existing behavior for already valid output paths or where the command writes its redirected output.

behavior: If `--out-file` points to a file inside a missing directory tree, the CLI creates the parent directories before writing the output file.
Relative `--out-file` paths that include subdirectories or parent-directory traversal remain valid and should be writable even when those directories are absent beforehand.
If the destination directory already exists, `--out-file` continues to work normally without introducing a new error condition.
After preparing the destination path, the command writes its redirected output to the requested file instead of requiring the caller to create the directory structure manually.
acceptance_criteria: When a command that supports `--out-file` is run with a nested file path whose parent folder does not exist, it should complete successfully and create both the folder and the output file.

When `--out-file` uses a relative path that includes parent-directory traversal and the destination folder does not exist, it should still create the needed folder and write the output file successfully.
When the parent directory already exists, using `--out-file` should continue to write the output file successfully with no regression in behavior.
When `--out-file` is only a filename in the current working directory, the command should behave the same as before.

task_37.title: Restore legacy GCC default version normalization
task_37.description: Conan 2.18.0 restores compatibility for auto-detected older GCC versions by using the legacy default version format. Pre-5 GCC releases now default to a major.minor compiler version even when the compiler reports a patch number, while newer GCC behavior remains unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that automatic GCC compiler version detection preserves legacy compatibility for older GCC releases by defaulting pre-5 versions to major.minor instead of full major.minor.patch values.

expectation.grounded: `default_compiler_version` should normalize detected `gcc` versions below 5 to `major.minor`. For `gcc` 5 and newer, it should continue returning only the major version. This preserves the existing default compiler version contract for older GCC while leaving separate full-version detection available.
expectation.conceptual: When Conan infers a GCC version for default settings, older GCC releases should be represented in the shortened form users historically received, while newer GCC releases should keep their current simplified version format.

constraints.grounded: Only the default version normalization for `gcc` below major version 5 should change. Existing default behavior for `gcc` 5 and newer and for other compilers must remain unchanged, and users must still be able to obtain a full compiler version through the dedicated full-version detection flow.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to preserving compatibility for older GCC defaults and must not alter how newer compiler versions or other compiler families are interpreted.

behavior: Auto-detected GCC versions with a major version lower than 5 now resolve to a default compiler version containing only major and minor components.
Patch components reported by older GCC releases are no longer included in the default compiler version value.
Auto-detected GCC versions 5 and newer continue to resolve to a major-only default compiler version.
Default version normalization for non-GCC compilers remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan auto-detects an older GCC release such as 4.9.3, it should use 4.9 as the default compiler version.
When Conan auto-detects GCC 5 or newer, it should continue using only the major version as the default compiler version.
When an older GCC installation reports a version including a patch number, the generated default compiler version should omit the patch component.
When detecting compilers other than GCC, their existing default version mapping behavior should remain unchanged.

task_35.title: Fix Windows LLVM/Clang runtime and clang-cl build flags
task_35.description: Conan 2.18.0 corrects Windows LLVM/Clang integration so GNU and Autotools toolchains generate the proper Debug dynamic runtime markers, and `clang-cl` uses MSVC-compatible build-type flags when configured as the frontend. This prevents Debug dynamic builds from behaving like release-runtime builds and aligns `clang-cl` behavior with MSVC-style expectations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Windows builds using LLVM/Clang through Conan generate the correct Debug dynamic MSVC runtime settings in `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain`, and ensure that `clang-cl` uses MSVC-compatible build-type flags instead of generic Clang/GNU-style flags when it is configured as the compiler frontend.

expectation.grounded: For `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain` on Windows, when the compiler flow is LLVM/Clang with `compiler.runtime=dynamic` and `compiler.runtime_type=Debug`, the generated runtime flags must include the debug runtime define in addition to the existing dynamic runtime markers and must keep selecting the debug MSVC runtime library. For non-Debug dynamic runtime, the release runtime selection must remain unchanged. In `build_type_flags(conanfile)`, detecting `clang-cl` from `tools.build:compiler_executables` must no longer force the Clang-specific build-type flag branch; that branch should only apply when the Visual Studio toolset itself is explicitly a Clang toolset, so `clang-cl` follows the MSVC-compatible mapping by default.
expectation.conceptual: Windows LLVM/Clang builds should keep Debug and Release runtime intent consistent across generated toolchains. Debug builds that use the dynamic MSVC runtime must behave like true debug-runtime builds, and `clang-cl` should inherit the same build-type semantics users expect from other MSVC-compatible frontends rather than GNU-style Clang defaults.

constraints.grounded: Do not change static-runtime behavior. Do not change non-Debug dynamic runtime selection beyond preserving the existing release-runtime linkage. Preserve the existing Clang-specific build-type flag path for explicit Clang Visual Studio toolsets, while leaving regular MSVC behavior and toolchain selection unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing non-debug and non-dynamic Windows toolchain behavior stable while fixing the mismatch in Debug dynamic runtime handling and `clang-cl` flag selection. The update should refine compatibility, not broaden behavior changes beyond the affected Windows LLVM/Clang scenarios.

behavior: Windows `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain` now distinguish Debug dynamic LLVM/Clang builds from other dynamic-runtime cases by adding the debug runtime define needed for debug MSVC C++ runtime linkage.

For Windows dynamic runtime builds with LLVM/Clang, Debug continues to target the debug MSVC runtime library and non-Debug continues to target the release MSVC runtime library, but Debug now exposes the additional debug marker expected by the runtime.

`build_type_flags(conanfile)` no longer treats `clang-cl` detected through `tools.build:compiler_executables` as a signal to use the Clang-specific build-type flag table; `clang-cl` now follows the MSVC-compatible build-type flag mapping unless the configured Visual Studio toolset explicitly indicates Clang.
acceptance_criteria: When a Windows package uses `AutotoolsToolchain` or `GnuToolchain` with LLVM/Clang, `compiler.runtime=dynamic`, and `compiler.runtime_type=Debug`, the generated compiler and runtime flags should indicate a debug dynamic MSVC runtime configuration rather than a release-style dynamic runtime configuration.

When the same Windows LLVM/Clang flow uses `compiler.runtime=dynamic` with a non-Debug runtime type, the generated runtime flags should continue to target the release MSVC runtime without introducing Debug-only markers.

When `clang-cl` is configured through `tools.build:compiler_executables`, Conan should derive Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo, and MinSizeRel build-type flags from the MSVC-compatible branch rather than the generic Clang/GNU branch, unless the active Visual Studio toolset is explicitly a Clang toolset.

When using existing MSVC or explicit Clang toolset configurations that were already selecting their corresponding build-type flag branches, behavior should remain consistent apart from the corrected Windows Debug dynamic runtime handling.

task_38.title: Restore source retrieval after resetting local recipe-index remotes
task_38.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes local recipe-index remotes so resetting or recreating the remote does not break later retrieval of exported recipe sources. When the remote's local index metadata has been lost, source lookup now recovers from the repository contents instead of failing solely because the index entry is missing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that resetting a local recipe-index remote does not break later retrieval of exported recipe sources for recipes resolved from that remote.

expectation.grounded: For local recipe-index remotes, when Conan needs recipe sources and the requested reference is no longer present in the remote's local index metadata, source retrieval should recover by resolving the recipe from the underlying repository content and using its exported sources. If the requested recipe is not actually available in that repository, Conan should continue to surface the normal not-found failure instead of returning sources.
expectation.conceptual: After a local recipe-index remote is recreated or reset, Conan should still be able to obtain the sources required by recipes stored in that remote. Users should only see a failure when the recipe truly does not exist, not because the remote's local metadata was rebuilt.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing successful source-retrieval path when the local recipe index already contains the requested recipe. The recovery path must only compensate for missing local index metadata and must not hide genuinely missing recipe references.
constraints.conceptual: Keep normal successful source downloads unchanged, and do not turn real missing-recipe situations into silent recovery.

behavior: When source retrieval from a local recipe-index remote cannot find the recipe in that remote's local index metadata, Conan falls back to recovering the recipe from the repository behind the remote.
Recovered source retrieval uses the recipe's exported sources, allowing install or build flows that depend on those sources to proceed after the remote has been reset.
If fallback recovery cannot find the requested recipe in the repository content, Conan still reports a not-found outcome.
Requests that already succeed through the existing local-index lookup continue to behave as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recipe stored in a local recipe-index remote, when the remote has been reset or recreated and Conan later needs that recipe's exported sources during an install or build, it should retrieve the sources and continue instead of failing solely because the local index metadata was lost.
Given a local recipe-index remote whose metadata still contains the requested recipe, when Conan retrieves recipe sources, it should behave the same as before the update.

Given a recipe reference that is absent from the underlying local recipe repository, when Conan tries to retrieve its sources from a local recipe-index remote, it should fail with the normal not-found behavior.
When a recipe relies on exported sources from a local recipe-index remote, resetting that remote should not by itself make those sources unavailable.

task_36.title: Fix Windows LLVM/Clang toolchain flags and Debug dynamic runtime
task_36.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes Windows LLVM/Clang toolchain generation in two places: GNU-based toolchains now emit the correct Debug dynamic-runtime settings for compiler=clang, and clang-cl is treated as an MSVC-compatible frontend when build-type flags are generated so MSVC-style flows such as NMake do not receive invalid option formats.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Windows LLVM/Clang builds are configured with the correct runtime and build-type flags: Debug dynamic-runtime builds generated by AutotoolsToolchain and GnuToolchain must link against the Debug MSVC runtime correctly, and clang-cl integrations must receive MSVC-compatible build-type options so MSVC-style workflows such as NMakeToolchain work without invalid flag translation.

expectation.grounded: For Windows profiles using compiler=clang, AutotoolsToolchain and GnuToolchain must distinguish the GNU-compatible LLVM/Clang frontend from clang-cl. When compiler.runtime is dynamic, runtime flag generation must select the appropriate MSVC dynamic runtime library and, when compiler.runtime_type is Debug, also define the debug runtime macro so the Debug MSVC C++ runtime is selected. When tools.build:compiler_executables points to clang-cl, build_type_flags() must return MSVC-compatible build-type options for Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo, and MinSizeRel instead of GNU-style clang options, so MSVC-formatted toolchains such as NMakeToolchain emit valid compiler arguments.
expectation.conceptual: Windows Clang support should distinguish between GNU-style clang and MSVC-style clang-cl. Debug builds that use the dynamic MSVC runtime should consistently select the debug runtime, and clang-cl builds should receive options in the format that MSVC-based generators expect.

constraints.grounded: Keep the existing non-Debug dynamic-runtime behavior that targets the release MSVC runtime. Do not change static-runtime handling. Preserve existing behavior for non-Windows GNU-style compilers and for standard MSVC build-type flag generation except where clang-cl detection requires MSVC-compatible flags.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be scoped to Windows LLVM/Clang interoperability and should not alter unrelated compiler families or runtime modes.

behavior: On Windows GNU-front-end LLVM/Clang builds generated by AutotoolsToolchain or GnuToolchain, dynamic Debug runtime configuration now includes the debug runtime define in addition to the existing dynamic-runtime defines and library selection, allowing linkage against the Debug MSVC runtime components.
On the same GNU-front-end LLVM/Clang path, dynamic non-Debug runtime configuration continues to target the non-Debug MSVC dynamic runtime without adding a debug-only define.

When tools.build:compiler_executables selects clang-cl, build-type flags are now produced in MSVC-compatible form for all standard build types, so MSVC-style generators such as NMakeToolchain no longer receive GNU-style clang build flags that become invalid when formatted as MSVC options.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Windows compiler=clang configuration using the GNU-compatible LLVM/Clang frontend with compiler.runtime=dynamic and compiler.runtime_type=Debug, when AutotoolsToolchain or GnuToolchain generates compiler flags, the resulting configuration should select the Debug MSVC dynamic runtime and define the debug runtime macro.

Given the same Windows GNU-front-end LLVM/Clang configuration with compiler.runtime=dynamic and a non-Debug runtime type, generated runtime flags should select the release MSVC dynamic runtime without adding debug-only runtime definitions.

Given a Windows compiler=clang profile where tools.build:compiler_executables sets the C/C++ compiler to clang-cl, when build-type flags are consumed by an MSVC-style generator such as NMakeToolchain, the generated compiler options should be valid MSVC-compatible build-type options for the selected build type.

When these Windows LLVM/Clang-specific conditions are not met, existing behavior for standard MSVC builds, static runtime configurations, and non-Windows GNU-style compiler flag generation should remain unchanged.

task_39.title: Correct Multi-Digit Compiler Version Detection
task_39.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes compiler auto-detection so GCC/Clang version parsing preserves full multi-digit version components. This prevents detected compiler settings from being truncated when the reported minor or later version segments contain more than one digit.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that compiler auto-detection preserves the full reported compiler version when a minor or later dotted component contains more than one digit, so detected settings do not shorten versions such as 8.12 or 15.15.0.

expectation.grounded: In detect_api, `_cc_compiler()` must accept dotted version components with multiple digits and return a `Version` built from the complete matched version token. `detect_gcc_compiler()` must also accept GCC version outputs with multi-digit minor values. For supported compiler banners, version extraction should continue preferring the actual compiler version token and should not include leading whitespace in the detected version value.
expectation.conceptual: Automatic compiler detection should report the full GCC/Clang version that the compiler exposes, rather than truncating multi-digit components. Users relying on detected compiler settings or generated profiles should see the same version number the compiler reports for supported formats.

constraints.grounded: Do not change compiler identification, executable selection, or the existing success/failure contract of detection calls. Major-only outputs, single-digit minor versions, and previously supported dotted versions must remain detectable; this update only broadens accepted numeric component widths and preserves a clean extracted version token.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing auto-detection behavior intact for already supported compiler outputs. The fix should only expand version parsing so larger numeric components are handled correctly without introducing false matches or formatting artifacts.

behavior: `_cc_compiler()` recognizes dotted versions whose minor and later components may contain more than one digit, instead of stopping after the first digit of those components.
When compiler banner output contains a version such as 15.15.0, `_cc_compiler()` returns a `Version` representing 15.15.0 rather than a truncated value such as 15.1.
`detect_gcc_compiler()` accepts GCC outputs with multi-digit minor versions such as 8.12 and returns the full detected version value.
The version token extracted by `_cc_compiler()` is normalized to the matched version text itself rather than including any leading space from the banner output.
acceptance_criteria: When compiler auto-detection reads a GCC or Clang banner that reports 15.15.0, it should identify the compiler correctly and report version 15.15.0, not 15.1.
When `detect_gcc_compiler()` receives GCC version output 8.12, it should return compiler `gcc`, version 8.12, and the selected executable name.
When detection receives supported major-only outputs such as 10 or 18, it should continue to succeed and report those versions unchanged.
When detection extracts a version from `cc` banner output, the reported version value should be the clean version token without leading whitespace artifacts.

task_41.title: Preserve ConanInvalidConfiguration from validation hooks
task_41.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes validation hook error handling so that ConanInvalidConfiguration raised during pre-validation or post-validation is treated as an invalid configuration outcome for package ID computation instead of being converted into a generic hook failure.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that raising ConanInvalidConfiguration from validation hooks marks the configuration as invalid instead of surfacing as a generic hook exception.

expectation.grounded: During run_validate_package_id, ConanInvalidConfiguration raised by HookManager.execute for the pre_validate or post_validate hooks must be forwarded unchanged and handled the same way as ConanFile.validate(), so the recipe is marked invalid instead of being converted into ConanException. The validation sequence should remain pre_validate, validate(), then post_validate, with post_validate only reached if no ConanInvalidConfiguration has already been raised.
expectation.conceptual: Validation hooks must be able to reject unsupported configurations using ConanInvalidConfiguration, and Conan should treat that outcome as a normal invalid-configuration result rather than an unexpected hook error.

constraints.grounded: Only ConanInvalidConfiguration receives this special forwarding behavior. Other exceptions raised by hooks must continue to be reported as hook execution failures wrapped as ConanException. Valid configurations must still execute pre_validate, validate(), and post_validate in order.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change normal hook failure handling for unrelated errors, and do not alter the standard validation flow for configurations that remain valid.

behavior: A pre_validate hook may raise ConanInvalidConfiguration to reject the current configuration, and Conan must treat that as an invalid package configuration outcome.
A post_validate hook may raise ConanInvalidConfiguration after validate() succeeds, and Conan must also treat that as an invalid package configuration outcome.
When ConanInvalidConfiguration is raised by pre_validate, validate(), or post_validate, Conan records the configuration as invalid instead of surfacing a generic hook exception.
Once ConanInvalidConfiguration is raised during validation processing, later validation stages are not executed.
Exceptions other than ConanInvalidConfiguration raised by validation hooks continue to be surfaced as hook-related ConanException failures.
acceptance_criteria: When a pre_validate hook raises ConanInvalidConfiguration, Conan should stop validation and report the configuration as an invalid package ID rather than as a generic hook error.
When validate() succeeds and post_validate raises ConanInvalidConfiguration, Conan should report the configuration as an invalid package ID rather than as a generic hook error.
When ConanInvalidConfiguration is raised during pre_validate, validate(), or post_validate, Conan should not continue to later validation steps.
When a validation hook raises an exception other than ConanInvalidConfiguration, Conan should continue reporting it as a hook execution error.

task_42.title: Handle tuple recipe generators with tool-provided generators
task_42.description: The 2.18.0 update fixes a Conan installation failure that occurred when a consumer recipe declared its `generators` as a tuple and a tool requirement also injected generators through `self.generator_info`. The upgrade preserves tool-require generator injection while allowing both generator sources to be combined and processed without crashing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing or creating a package does not crash when a recipe declares `generators` as a tuple and a tool requirement contributes additional generators through `self.generator_info`, and ensure that both sets of generators are still honored.

expectation.grounded: When Conan collects generators, if a build or tool requirement exposes `generator_info` and the consuming recipe's `conanfile.generators` is a tuple, Conan should merge the tool-provided generators with the recipe-defined generators without failing due to an incompatible sequence type. The existing warning that a tool-require is adding generators should still be emitted, and the merged generator list should continue to include the tool-provided generators before the recipe's own generators.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to combine recipe-declared generators and tool-require-provided generators regardless of whether the recipe expresses its generators as a tuple or another sequence. Package installation should proceed normally, with all expected generators still applied and the usual warning behavior preserved.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the meaning of `self.generator_info` injection for tool requirements. Do not remove the warning emitted when a tool requirement adds generators. Do not alter the effective ordering in which tool-provided generators are prepended ahead of the recipe's declared generators. Existing behavior for recipes whose `generators` are already list-like must remain compatible.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should remove only the crash condition for tuple-declared generators. It should not otherwise change which generators run, the order in which combined generators are considered, or the visible warning that informs users about tool-require generator injection.

behavior: Conan now accepts a recipe `generators` declaration expressed as a tuple when merging it with generators supplied by a tool requirement through `self.generator_info`.
Generator collection no longer fails because of a sequence-type mismatch when tool-require generators are combined with tuple-declared recipe generators.
When a tool requirement contributes generators, Conan still emits the warning indicating that the tool requirement is adding generators.
The combined generator set preserves the existing prepend semantics: tool-require generators are considered before the recipe's own declared generators.
acceptance_criteria: When a package recipe declares `generators` as a tuple and a tool requirement contributes generators through `self.generator_info`, installing or creating the package should not crash during generator collection.
When both the recipe and a tool requirement define generators, Conan should retain both sources in the effective generator set rather than dropping either one.
When tool-require generators are injected, Conan should still surface the warning that the tool requirement is adding generators.
When a recipe does not use tuple-declared generators, existing generator injection behavior should remain unchanged.

task_40.title: Adopt package-oriented Conan workspace orchestration
task_40.description: Conan 2.18.0 removes the separate workspace product concept and changes workspace orchestration to operate on workspace packages. `conan workspace build` now computes dependency order across selected packages, a new ordered `conan workspace install` performs per-package installs, and the previous monolithic install behavior moves to `conan workspace super-install`. Workspace definitions and generated scaffolds now represent packages as `path`/`ref` entries instead of a `products` section.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that workspace workflows no longer depend on a separate product definition, and that users can add, inspect, install, and build workspace packages using package-based orchestration that respects dependency order. Ensure that monolithic workspace installation remains available under the dedicated `conan workspace super-install` command.

expectation.grounded: In Conan 2.18.0, `conan workspace add` should register workspace packages without a `--product` option, workspace metadata should expose only `packages`, and workspace definitions should store each package as a `path` plus `ref` entry. `conan workspace build` and `conan workspace install` should select all workspace packages or the subset matched by repeated `--pkg` reference patterns, compute a merged dependency/build order from the selected package graphs, and then run the corresponding per-package `conan build` or `conan install` operations in that order. `conan workspace build` should automatically include `editable` in build mode when not already requested. The previous collapsed, single-result workspace install flow should be invoked through `conan workspace super-install` instead of `conan workspace install`.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, workspaces should behave as a package-oriented orchestration feature rather than a product-oriented one. Users should be able to build or install either the whole workspace or selected workspace packages, and Conan should process them in dependency order automatically. The command named `workspace install` should now mean ordered per-package installation, while the old one-shot workspace-wide install remains available under `workspace super-install`.

constraints.grounded: Package selection should be based on workspace package references matched via `--pkg`; if no workspace package is selected, the command should fail instead of running with an empty set. Workspace package entries should preserve declared `output_folder` and reference identity for the per-package command invocations. Packages already present in the workspace should not be duplicated when re-added by the same path. External dependencies should only be built when binary analysis marks them for build under the requested build mode; otherwise the ordered workspace flow should rely on normal install behavior for non-workspace dependencies.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should not require users to maintain a separate list of build targets inside the workspace. Selection must stay explicit and predictable, partial package operations must not silently act on unrelated workspace packages, and existing workspace-specific output locations should continue to apply. Dependency orchestration should extend to external packages only when Conan determines they need to be built.

behavior: Workspace definitions and generated workspace templates use a package list made of `ref` and `path` entries, and no longer expose a separate `products` section.
`conan workspace add` no longer accepts a product designation and treats every added entry as a workspace package.
`conan workspace info` reports workspace packages without a `products` field.
`conan workspace build` computes dependency order across workspace packages instead of starting from declared products.
`conan workspace build` automatically enables editable builds when the caller did not already request `--build=editable`.
`conan workspace build` and the new `conan workspace install` accept repeated `--pkg` selectors to restrict orchestration to matching package references.
If `--pkg` selectors do not match any workspace package, the workspace command fails instead of proceeding with no targets.

When binary analysis determines that an external dependency must be built, the ordered workspace build flow triggers the required external build/install step before continuing with dependent workspace packages.
The previous monolithic workspace install behavior is exposed via `conan workspace super-install`, while `conan workspace install` now runs ordered per-package installs.
acceptance_criteria: Given a workspace with package dependencies among workspace members, when the user runs `conan workspace build` without selectors, Conan should build workspace packages in dependency order without requiring any separate product list.
When the user runs `conan workspace add` for a package, the package should become part of the workspace package set without any `--product` flag or product-specific metadata.

When the user inspects or generates a workspace definition, the visible workspace package data should be represented as package entries containing a reference and path, and there should be no separate products list.

When the user runs `conan workspace build` or `conan workspace install` with one or more `--pkg` selectors, Conan should only orchestrate workspace packages whose references match those selectors; if none match, the command should fail.
When the user runs `conan workspace build` without explicitly requesting editable builds, editable workspace packages should still be built as part of the ordered workflow.

When the user needs the old single-result workspace install behavior, `conan workspace super-install` should perform that collapsed workspace installation, while `conan workspace install` should perform the per-package ordered install flow.

task_43.title: Fix Meson architecture mapping for riscv64
task_43.description: Conan 2.18.0 corrects Meson toolchain architecture detection so 64-bit RISC-V targets are emitted with the right CPU metadata and 64-bit WebAssembly targets are recognized explicitly. This prevents affected Meson configurations from describing the target architecture incorrectly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Meson toolchain generation reports the correct target CPU information for 64-bit RISC-V builds and recognizes 64-bit WebAssembly targets so generated Meson machine definitions match the requested architecture.

expectation.grounded: When `MesonToolchain` derives Meson machine information from Conan settings, `arch=riscv64` must map to Meson CPU family `riscv64`, CPU `riscv64`, and little-endian semantics instead of mixing 64-bit and 32-bit RISC-V identifiers. `arch=wasm64` must also be recognized and mapped to Meson CPU family `wasm64`, CPU `wasm64`, and little-endian semantics.
