expectation.conceptual: Generating a Meson toolchain for a 64-bit RISC-V target should identify that target consistently as 64-bit RISC-V, and 64-bit WebAssembly targets should be treated as supported named architectures rather than falling back to incorrect architecture metadata.

constraints.grounded: Existing Meson architecture mappings for unaffected targets must retain their current CPU family, CPU, and endianness values. The observable scope of this update is limited to correcting the `riscv64` mapping and adding explicit `wasm64` coverage.
constraints.conceptual: The update should be narrowly scoped to accurate architecture reporting and must not change behavior for unrelated target architectures.

behavior: A Meson toolchain generated for a `riscv64` target now emits `riscv64` as both the Meson CPU family and CPU value while keeping little-endian reporting.
The previous misidentification of `riscv64` targets as 32-bit RISC-V in part of the generated Meson architecture metadata is removed.
`wasm64` is now explicitly recognized by the Meson architecture mapper and emitted as `wasm64` little-endian machine metadata.
acceptance_criteria: When `MesonToolchain` is generated for a target with `arch=riscv64`, the resulting Meson machine configuration should identify the target CPU family as `riscv64`.

When `MesonToolchain` is generated for a target with `arch=riscv64`, the resulting Meson machine configuration should identify the target CPU as `riscv64` and should not report a 32-bit RISC-V variant for the same target.
When `MesonToolchain` is generated for a target with `arch=wasm64`, the resulting Meson machine configuration should use `wasm64` target CPU metadata.
When `MesonToolchain` is generated for unaffected supported architectures such as `riscv32`, their existing Meson CPU metadata should remain unchanged.

task_44.title: Scope Apple ARC flags to Objective-C toolchains
task_44.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes Apple toolchain flag generation so Automatic Reference Counting configuration is emitted only for Objective-C and Objective-C++ compilation paths instead of being mixed into generic C, C++, and linker flags. This keeps Apple-specific bitcode and visibility behavior intact while preventing ARC-only switches from leaking into unrelated languages.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Apple ARC configuration affects only Objective-C and Objective-C++ build settings, and that generic C, C++, and linker settings no longer receive ARC-specific switches when generating toolchains for Apple targets.

expectation.grounded: When `tools.apple:enable_arc` is configured, Conan 2.18.0 should stop contributing `-fobjc-arc` or `-fno-objc-arc` through the shared Apple extra flag set used by generic C/C++ outputs. `CMakeToolchain` generation should expose ARC only through `CONAN_OBJC_FLAGS` and `CONAN_OBJCXX_FLAGS`, and those values should initialize `CMAKE_OBJC_FLAGS_INIT` and `CMAKE_OBJCXX_FLAGS_INIT`; `CONAN_C_FLAGS` and `CONAN_CXX_FLAGS` should contain only the non-ARC Apple flags. `MesonToolchain`, `GnuToolchain`, and `AutotoolsToolchain` should place the ARC selection only in Objective-C-specific outputs such as `objc_args`, `objcpp_args`, `OBJCFLAGS`, and `OBJCXXFLAGS`, while `c_args`, `cpp_args`, `CFLAGS`, `CXXFLAGS`, and `LDFLAGS` remain free of ARC switches.
expectation.conceptual: On Apple builds, enabling or disabling ARC should change only Objective-C and Objective-C++ compilation behavior. Shared C/C++ compiler settings and linker settings should still receive other Apple-related options such as bitcode or visibility, but they should not carry ARC-only flags.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing Apple bitcode and visibility handling, including the debug and non-debug bitcode variants. Do not inject ARC into generic C, C++, or linker outputs for any supported generator. Objective-C and Objective-C++ outputs must continue to receive the shared non-ARC Apple and compiler/linker flags in addition to the ARC choice when applicable.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing Apple platform flag behavior intact except for removing ARC from language-agnostic outputs. The change must not drop other shared Apple build settings, and it must not add ARC anywhere outside Objective-C and Objective-C++ compilation channels.

behavior: Apple ARC enable/disable is removed from the common Apple flag set and no longer propagates into generic C, C++, or linker flags.

CMake toolchain generation now separates Objective-C and Objective-C++ Apple flags into `CONAN_OBJC_FLAGS` and `CONAN_OBJCXX_FLAGS`, and maps them to `CMAKE_OBJC_FLAGS_INIT` and `CMAKE_OBJCXX_FLAGS_INIT`.
Meson toolchain generation adds the ARC switch only to `objc_args` and `objcpp_args`, while keeping generic `c_args`, `cpp_args`, `c_link_args`, and `cpp_link_args` non-ARC.
Meson Objective-C and Objective-C++ outputs inherit the corresponding shared C/C++ compile and link flags so non-ARC Apple settings are preserved alongside the Objective-C-specific ARC selection.
GNU and Autotools toolchain generation now emits ARC only through `OBJCFLAGS` and `OBJCXXFLAGS`; `CFLAGS`, `CXXFLAGS`, and `LDFLAGS` keep only the non-ARC Apple flags.
acceptance_criteria: When an Apple target is generated with `tools.apple:enable_arc=True`, generic C and C++ toolchain outputs should include applicable Apple bitcode and visibility flags but should not include `-fobjc-arc`.
When an Apple target is generated with `tools.apple:enable_arc=True`, the generator-specific Objective-C and Objective-C++ flag outputs should include `-fobjc-arc`.

When an Apple target is generated with `tools.apple:enable_arc=False`, the generator-specific Objective-C and Objective-C++ flag outputs should include `-fno-objc-arc`, and generic C, C++, and linker outputs should remain free of ARC switches.

When generating CMake toolchains for Apple targets, Objective-C and Objective-C++ initial CMake flag variables should receive the Apple ARC choice without adding that ARC choice to the generic C and C++ initial flag variables.

When generating Meson, GNU, or Autotools toolchains for Apple targets, Objective-C and Objective-C++ outputs should preserve the same non-ARC shared Apple/compiler/linker settings as the corresponding C/C++ outputs, with ARC added only to the Objective-C-specific compile flag channels.

task_45.title: Fix mocked HEAD request handling in TestClient
task_45.description: Version 2.18.0 fixes a bug in TestClient's mocked HTTP handling so HEAD requests against existing resources return a proper successful HTTP response instead of a non-response success value. This makes mocked HEAD-based existence checks behave consistently with expected HTTP semantics while preserving not-found behavior for missing resources.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that mocked HEAD requests made through TestClient behave correctly, so users can rely on HEAD-based existence checks in mocked client flows for both existing and missing resources.

expectation.grounded: TestClient mocked HEAD requests should produce a valid successful HTTP response for existing targets and continue to surface a 404-style not-found outcome for missing targets. Successful HEAD handling should be observable through normal HTTP response semantics rather than a generic truthy return value.
expectation.conceptual: When a user performs a mocked HEAD request through TestClient, it should behave like a real HTTP HEAD call: existing resources succeed with a normal success response, and missing resources report not found.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable not-found behavior for absent resources; mocked HEAD requests should still fail as 404 when the target does not exist. The fix should only normalize the successful HEAD path so callers do not need special-case handling for malformed success results.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the missing-resource behavior unchanged while making successful mocked HEAD requests reliable and standards-aligned from the caller's perspective.

behavior: A mocked HEAD request to an existing resource now yields a proper HTTP success response with status 200.
A mocked HEAD request to a missing resource continues to yield a not-found error outcome.
Code that uses TestClient mocked HEAD requests for resource availability checks can depend on standard HTTP success-versus-not-found behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When TestClient performs a mocked HEAD request for a resource that exists, it should complete with an HTTP 200 success response.
When TestClient performs a mocked HEAD request for a resource that does not exist, it should report a 404 not-found outcome.

When application code uses mocked HEAD requests to determine whether a resource is present, it should be able to rely on normal HTTP response semantics without interpreting non-response sentinel values.

task_46.title: Scope Conan core configuration to internal use
task_46.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes configuration scoping so `core.xxx` values supplied through `global.conf` or `-cc` remain internal to Conan instead of leaking into profile or recipe-visible configuration, while normal non-core configuration inheritance continues unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `core.xxx` configuration supplied through `global.conf` or `-cc` is treated as Conan-internal only and does not leak into profiles or recipe-visible configuration.

expectation.grounded: When Conan combines global configuration with profile configuration, any `core.xxx` entries originating from `global.conf` or CLI `-cc` must be excluded from the resulting profile-scoped configuration. Recipes and profiles should continue to receive non-`core` configuration through the normal merge process.
expectation.conceptual: Global internal settings should stay internal. Upgrading to 2.18.0 should stop `core` options from affecting recipe-facing profile configuration, without changing how ordinary user configuration is inherited.

constraints.grounded: Filter only `core.xxx` configuration during global-to-profile composition; do not drop, rename, or alter non-`core` conf entries inherited from global sources. The change must preserve existing profile behavior for regular conf keys.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be narrowly scoped to internal Conan settings and must not break existing configuration inheritance for normal user options.

behavior: Global configuration rebased into profiles omits any `core.xxx` conf entries.
CLI `-cc` values targeting `core.xxx` are not exposed as profile or recipe configuration.
Non-`core` configuration from `global.conf` or CLI config continues to propagate into profiles as before.
acceptance_criteria: When `global.conf` contains both `core.xxx` and non-`core` keys and a profile is resolved, the profile-visible configuration should contain only the non-`core` entries.
When a user passes `-cc core.xxx=...` while running a Conan command, that setting should remain internal to Conan and should not be observable as profile configuration in recipes.
When a user passes non-`core` configuration through `global.conf` or `-cc`, it should still be inherited by profiles and remain visible to recipes as before.

task_48.title: Fix `conan export-pkg` version string handling
task_48.description: Version 2.18.0 fixes `conan export-pkg` so recipe code receives the package version as a plain string during export. This removes an inconsistency with other Conan command flows and prevents recipes from failing when they rely on `self.version` having normal string behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan export-pkg` exposes the conanfile version as a string during recipe evaluation so package export remains consistent with other Conan CLI flows and recipes do not fail because `self.version` is provided as a non-string type.

expectation.grounded: When `conan export-pkg` is invoked with a package version, the recipe should observe `self.version` as a Python `str` throughout the command's recipe execution, including callbacks such as `requirements()`. The command should use the CLI-facing string form of the version instead of passing a wrapped reference version type into the conanfile.
expectation.conceptual: `conan export-pkg` should present the version to recipe code exactly as users typed it, so recipes can treat `self.version` like a normal string and behave the same way they do in other Conan commands.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the `conan export-pkg` command surface, reference syntax, or broader export flow. Limit the fix to the observable type of the version value seen by recipe code, and keep it aligned with the existing Conan behavior that passes CLI version values as strings in comparable flows.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should remove the version-type inconsistency without introducing new command options or changing how users specify package coordinates.

behavior: `conan export-pkg` now normalizes the resolved recipe version to a plain string before the conanfile consumes it.
Recipe methods executed during `conan export-pkg`, including dependency declaration logic, observe `self.version` as a string rather than a specialized version object.
Recipes that depend on string semantics for `self.version`, such as exact type checks or standard string operations, no longer fail solely because they are being run under `conan export-pkg`.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recipe that expects `self.version` to be a Python string during `requirements()`, when `conan export-pkg` is run with an explicit version, the command should complete without failing because the version has a non-string type.
When recipe logic compares, concatenates, or otherwise uses `self.version` as a string during `conan export-pkg`, it should behave consistently with other Conan CLI commands that accept `--version`.
When users upgrade to 2.18.0, they should not need to change recipe code or command syntax merely to handle a different `self.version` type in `conan export-pkg`.

task_47.title: Honor Apple-specific deployment targets in XcodeToolchain
task_47.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes XcodeToolchain so generated Xcode settings use the correct deployment target variable for each supported Apple platform. This makes the configured minimum OS version apply correctly for iOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS builds instead of treating all platforms like macOS.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that XcodeToolchain applies the configured minimum deployment version through the correct Apple-platform deployment target setting for each supported OS, so Xcode builds honor os.version consistently on macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS.

expectation.grounded: When XcodeToolchain generates Xcode configuration values and settings.os.version is present, it should emit the deployment target assignment that matches settings.os: MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for Macos, IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for iOS, TVOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for tvOS, WATCHOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for watchOS, and XROS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for visionOS. The assigned value should be the configured os.version, and any existing configuration-conditional suffix behavior should remain applied to that assignment.
expectation.conceptual: XcodeToolchain should make Xcode honor the minimum supported OS version for each Apple platform by exposing the correct platform-specific deployment target setting whenever a deployment version is configured.

constraints.grounded: Do not change unrelated generated toolchain settings such as the C++ library or C++ language standard entries. If settings.os.version is absent, XcodeToolchain should continue omitting a deployment target assignment. The change should only affect which Apple deployment target variable name is emitted for supported Apple operating systems.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to deployment target selection, leave unrelated toolchain output unchanged, preserve configuration scoping behavior, and remain a no-op when no deployment version is specified.

behavior: XcodeToolchain continues to emit MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for Macos builds when os.version is configured.

XcodeToolchain now emits IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, TVOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, WATCHOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, or XROS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for iOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS builds respectively when os.version is configured.
The deployment target value written to generated Xcode configuration output is taken from settings.os.version.
Any configuration-conditional suffix applied to generated Xcode settings remains attached to the deployment target assignment.
If no os.version is configured, no deployment target assignment is generated.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recipe that uses XcodeToolchain with os=Macos and os.version set, when the toolchain is generated, the resulting Xcode configuration should expose that version through MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET.

Given a recipe that uses XcodeToolchain with os=iOS, os=tvOS, os=watchOS, or os=visionOS and os.version set, when the toolchain is generated, the resulting Xcode configuration should expose that version through the corresponding platform deployment target variable instead of the macOS deployment target variable.
When XcodeToolchain generation is scoped by Xcode configuration, the emitted deployment target assignment should retain the same configuration-specific scoping.
When os.version is not provided, XcodeToolchain generation should not add any Apple deployment target assignment.

task_51.title: Respect folders.root during source() path resolution
task_51.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes local source path resolution so recipes that define a custom layout root use that rooted location during source() instead of always resolving from the recipe directory.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that recipes using layout() with a defined folders.root have source() and its source-related paths resolved from the rooted layout location rather than from the recipe directory.

expectation.grounded: When a Conan recipe defines layout() and sets conanfile.folders.root, the local source step must resolve its base folder from recipe_folder combined with folders.root, normalized as a path, before deriving source_folder and other source-related recipe locations exposed during conanfile.source(). If folders.root is not set, source resolution must continue to use recipe_folder.
expectation.conceptual: Recipes that opt into a custom layout root should see the source step operate from that rooted workspace, so source files are read from or written to the expected location instead of an unrooted recipe directory.

constraints.grounded: Do not change behavior for recipes that leave folders.root unset. Relative root values must resolve predictably against the recipe directory, including parent-directory roots, and all source-related folder properties exposed during the local source step must remain internally consistent with the same effective base location.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing unrooted recipes working as before, and only alter behavior for recipes that explicitly define a custom root. Rooted layouts should behave consistently even when the root points outside the recipe directory.

behavior: If layout() sets folders.root, the local source step uses the normalized combination of the recipe directory and folders.root as its base folder.
The source_folder observed during source() is derived from that rooted base instead of always being derived from the recipe directory.
Other source-related recipe locations exposed during the local source step, including export-sources resolution, follow the same rooted base when folders.root is present.
Recipes that do not define folders.root continue to resolve source-related paths from the recipe directory with no behavioral change.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe defines layout() with folders.root and folders.source, invoking the local source step should make source() operate against the rooted source directory that combines those layout settings.
When folders.root points to a parent or sibling-relative location, the source step should resolve that location as a normalized path relative to the recipe directory.
When source() reads source-related folder properties during execution, those properties should all reflect the same rooted base location.
When a recipe does not set folders.root, invoking the source step should behave the same as in the previous version.

task_50.title: Fix repeated Conan CMake package discovery in nested directories
task_50.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes a CMake dependency-generation issue so the same package can be discovered multiple times with find_package() from parent folders and subfolders without breaking target configuration, while preserving transitive system-library linkage for generated imported targets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan-generated CMake package configuration files can be used with multiple `find_package()` calls across parent folders and subfolders without causing target reconfiguration problems, and that package-declared system libraries remain part of the imported target's transitive link requirements.

expectation.grounded: For `CMakeConfigDeps`-generated package configs, repeated `find_package(<pkg> CONFIG ...)` calls for the same Conan dependency in different directories of one CMake configure pass should behave idempotently and leave the imported Conan targets usable. Packages that declare `cpp_info.system_libs` must continue to expose those libraries through the generated target interface, with configuration-aware resolution consistent with the active CMake configuration.
expectation.conceptual: Calling `find_package()` for the same Conan package from multiple `CMakeLists.txt` files in a project tree should just work. The imported package target should remain stable and should still carry the system libraries consumers need to link successfully.

constraints.grounded: Existing consumer `find_package()` usage and Conan-generated target names must remain compatible. Scenarios that already work with a single package discovery must keep the same dependency exposure, and repeated package discovery must not drop, duplicate, or mis-scope system-library link requirements across configurations.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should remove the duplicate-discovery failure mode without forcing consumers to rewrite their CMake usage or changing the dependency contract of package resolutions that already behaved correctly.

behavior: Conan-generated CMake target configuration files are safe to process more than once, so repeated `find_package()` calls for the same package in parent and nested directories no longer re-run conflicting target setup.
System libraries declared by a Conan package remain attached to the generated imported target as transitive interface link requirements.
System-library link requirements follow the active CMake configuration in the same way as other configuration-scoped Conan link interface entries.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer project calls `find_package(<pkg> CONFIG REQUIRED)` for the same Conan package in a top-level CMake file and again in a subdirectory, CMake configuration should complete without duplicate target declaration or conflicting Conan target setup behavior.
When the discovered Conan package declares system libraries, a consumer target linking against the Conan imported target should inherit those system-library requirements transitively.

When Conan generates configuration-specific package information, the system-library requirements exposed by the imported target should match the active build configuration after repeated package discovery.

task_49.title: Honor core-conf overrides in cache backup uploads
task_49.description: Conan 2.18.0 fixes `conan cache backup-upload` so command-line `-cc` and `--core-conf` overrides are actually parsed and applied. This lets users run backup uploads with temporary core configuration, including backup source location and upload settings, instead of having those arguments silently ignored.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache backup-upload` honors `-cc` and `--core-conf` overrides so users can run source-backup uploads with temporary Conan core configuration instead of relying only on persisted settings.

expectation.grounded: The `conan cache backup-upload` command must parse its CLI arguments and apply `-cc` and `--core-conf` values before collecting and uploading backup source files. Core configuration overrides relevant to backup uploads, including settings that affect the backup source cache, the upload destination, and source exclusion rules, must influence the command's runtime behavior instead of being ignored.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to pass temporary core configuration directly to the backup-upload command and have the upload behave as if those settings were active for that invocation. The command should no longer act as though no override was provided.

constraints.grounded: This change should only correct argument handling for `conan cache backup-upload`. The command must keep its existing purpose of uploading all backup sources currently available in the active cache scope, still respecting configured exclusions, and runs without `-cc` or `--core-conf` must retain their prior behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should preserve the command's existing default workflow and scope. Only the missing application of user-supplied runtime configuration should change; default executions should continue to behave the same.

behavior: `conan cache backup-upload` now participates in normal CLI argument parsing for the command invocation.
`-cc` and `--core-conf` values supplied to `conan cache backup-upload` now affect the backup upload operation at runtime.
Temporary core configuration can change which backup source files are discovered for upload and which destination the command uses for that upload.
Exclusion-related core configuration provided at invocation time is honored during backup source selection instead of being silently ignored.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan cache backup-upload` is invoked with `-cc` or `--core-conf` values that change the backup source cache location, it should use that overridden location for the current upload operation.

When the command is invoked with `-cc` or `--core-conf` values that define the backup upload destination, it should perform the upload using that destination without requiring the same setting to already exist in persistent Conan configuration.
When the command is invoked with `-cc` or `--core-conf` values that exclude specific source origins from backup, those excluded sources should not be uploaded in that invocation.
When the command is invoked without any `-cc` or `--core-conf` overrides, it should preserve the pre-existing backup-upload behavior.
